cards.front: Define Lattice in the context of Solid State Physics.
cards.back: An infinite periodic set of points generated by integer combinations of primitive translation vectors.

cards.front: Define Basis in the context of Solid State Physics.
cards.back: The atom or group of atoms attached identically to every lattice point.

cards.front: Define Crystal structure in the context of Solid State Physics.
cards.back: Lattice plus basis; the lattice alone does not specify which atoms occupy the structure.

cards.front: Define Primitive cell in the context of Solid State Physics.
cards.back: A repeating cell containing exactly one lattice point in the counting sense; it need not display the highest symmetry.

cards.front: Define Reciprocal lattice in the context of Solid State Physics.
cards.back: The set of wavevectors G satisfying exp(iG·R)=1 for every direct-lattice translation R.

cards.front: Define Miller indices (hkl) in the context of Solid State Physics.
cards.back: Integers proportional to reciprocals of a plane’s intercepts with the crystallographic axes.

cards.front: Define Brillouin zone in the context of Solid State Physics.
cards.back: A Wigner–Seitz cell of the reciprocal lattice; the first zone contains inequivalent crystal wavevectors.

cards.front: Define Bloch state in the context of Solid State Physics.
cards.back: An eigenstate in a periodic potential of the form ψₙₖ(r)=uₙₖ(r)e^{ik·r}, where u has lattice periodicity.

cards.front: Define Band gap in the context of Solid State Physics.
cards.back: An energy interval with no allowed bulk electronic states between occupied and unoccupied bands for the stated model and conditions.

cards.front: Define Fermi level in the context of Solid State Physics.
cards.back: The chemical potential for electrons; at zero temperature it equals the highest occupied energy for an ideal fermion ground state.

cards.front: Define Effective mass in the context of Solid State Physics.
cards.back: A band-curvature parameter defined through 1/m*=(1/ħ²)d²E/dk² in one dimension; it describes carrier acceleration within a band model.

cards.front: Define Phonon in the context of Solid State Physics.
cards.back: A quantum of a normal mode of lattice vibration; it is a collective excitation, not a localized atom.

cards.front: Define Point defect in the context of Solid State Physics.
cards.back: A localized departure from ideal occupancy, such as a vacancy, interstitial, or substitution.

cards.front: Define Dislocation in the context of Solid State Physics.
cards.back: A line defect characterized by a Burgers vector and associated long-range strain field.

cards.front: Define Crystallite versus grain in the context of Solid State Physics.
cards.back: A crystallite is a coherently diffracting domain. A grain is a microstructural region separated by grain boundaries and can contain subgrains or domains.

cards.front: Define Accuracy in the context of Materials Characterization.
cards.back: Closeness to an accepted/reference value under stated conditions; it depends on bias and calibration.

cards.front: Define Precision in the context of Materials Characterization.
cards.back: Closeness of repeated values to one another; high precision does not guarantee low bias.

cards.front: Define Resolution in the context of Materials Characterization.
cards.back: Ability to distinguish nearby spatial, spectral, temporal, angular, or energy features; always name the domain.

cards.front: Define Sensitivity in the context of Materials Characterization.
cards.back: Change in output per change in measurand, often the slope of a calibration curve.

cards.front: Define Selectivity in the context of Materials Characterization.
cards.back: Ability to respond to the desired measurand despite interferents or cross-sensitivities.

cards.front: Define Calibration in the context of Materials Characterization.
cards.back: Establishing the relationship between instrument indication and reference values, including uncertainty and conditions.

cards.front: Define Detection limit in the context of Materials Characterization.
cards.back: A procedure-defined smallest signal/amount distinguishable from background at stated error probabilities; not simply zero plus one standard deviation.

cards.front: Define Sampling volume/depth in the context of Materials Characterization.
cards.back: Region contributing appreciably to the signal; it depends on probe energy, interaction, material, geometry, and detection.

cards.front: Define Artifact in the context of Materials Characterization.
cards.back: A feature introduced or altered by preparation, instrument, environment, acquisition, or processing rather than intrinsic sample behavior.

cards.front: Define Reference/blank in the context of Materials Characterization.
cards.back: A standard or background measurement used to calibrate, normalize, or separate non-sample contributions.

cards.front: Define Repeatability in the context of Materials Characterization.
cards.back: Agreement under the same method, operator, instrument, location, and short time interval.

cards.front: Define Reproducibility in the context of Materials Characterization.
cards.back: Agreement when relevant conditions such as operator, instrument, laboratory, or batch change.

cards.front: Define Traceability in the context of Materials Characterization.
cards.back: An unbroken documented chain of calibrations linking a result to stated references, each with uncertainty.

cards.front: Define Quantification in the context of Materials Characterization.
cards.back: Estimating a value through a stated model, calibration, corrections, uncertainty, and validity range—not merely reading a peak.

cards.front: Define Complementary evidence in the context of Materials Characterization.
cards.back: Independent or differently sensitive measurements that test separate parts of a claim or competing explanation.

cards.front: Define Refractive index in the context of Optics and Lasers.
cards.back: For a specified frequency and medium, phase index n=c/v_p; it can be dispersive and complex in absorbing media.

cards.front: Define Optical path length in the context of Optics and Lasers.
cards.back: The path integral ∫n ds; relative optical path determines phase accumulation for monochromatic light.

cards.front: Define Paraxial approximation in the context of Optics and Lasers.
cards.back: Rays stay close to the optical axis and make small angles, allowing sinθ≈tanθ≈θ and linearized imaging.

cards.front: Define Coherence in the context of Optics and Lasers.
cards.back: Statistical stability of phase correlation in time or space; it is quantified by correlation functions, not simply an on/off property.

cards.front: Define Interference in the context of Optics and Lasers.
cards.back: Redistribution of intensity caused by superposition of mutually coherent field amplitudes.

cards.front: Define Diffraction in the context of Optics and Lasers.
cards.back: Wave propagation effects associated with finite apertures/obstacles; in the far field the pattern reflects the aperture’s spatial spectrum.

cards.front: Define Polarization in the context of Optics and Lasers.
cards.back: The state describing the trajectory/statistics of the transverse electric-field vector.

cards.front: Define Numerical aperture in the context of Optics and Lasers.
cards.back: NA=n sinθ_max for an imaging or collection cone in a medium of index n.

cards.front: Define Resolving power in the context of Optics and Lasers.
cards.back: Ability to distinguish nearby spatial or spectral features under a declared criterion; it is not magnification.

cards.front: Define Population inversion in the context of Optics and Lasers.
cards.back: A nonequilibrium condition with more population in an upper laser level than a lower one after degeneracy is treated appropriately.

cards.front: Define Stimulated emission in the context of Optics and Lasers.
cards.back: An incident field induces emission into a mode coherent with that field in frequency, phase, direction, and polarization under the transition model.

cards.front: Define Laser threshold in the context of Optics and Lasers.
cards.back: The gain condition at which round-trip amplification balances internal and output-coupling losses.

cards.front: Define Quantum efficiency in the context of Optics and Lasers.
cards.back: Ratio of collected charge carriers or counts to incident photons under stated wavelength and operating conditions.

cards.front: Define Responsivity in the context of Optics and Lasers.
cards.back: Electrical output per incident optical power, commonly A/W for a photodiode.

cards.front: Define Dark current in the context of Optics and Lasers.
cards.back: Detector current present without intended illumination, dependent on temperature, bias, area, and device physics.

cards.front: Define System and boundary in the context of Thermodynamics.
cards.back: The chosen matter/region and its separating surface; boundary may allow energy and/or matter transfer depending on the model.

cards.front: Define State function in the context of Thermodynamics.
cards.back: A property determined by equilibrium state, so its differential is exact and its change is path independent.

cards.front: Define Heat in the context of Thermodynamics.
cards.back: Energy transferred across a boundary because of a temperature difference; it is not a substance stored in a body.

cards.front: Define Work in the context of Thermodynamics.
cards.back: Organized energy transfer associated with generalized force–displacement variables; boundary work is only one form.

cards.front: Define Quasistatic process in the context of Thermodynamics.
cards.back: A process slow enough to pass through states arbitrarily close to equilibrium; it can still be irreversible through friction, viscosity, finite gradients, or hysteresis.

cards.front: Define Reversible process in the context of Thermodynamics.
cards.back: An ideal process that can be reversed with system and surroundings restored and no net entropy generation.

cards.front: Define Entropy in the context of Thermodynamics.
cards.back: A state function satisfying dS=δQ_rev/T for a reversible path and ΔS_universe≥0 for an isolated total system.

cards.front: Define Enthalpy in the context of Thermodynamics.
cards.back: H=U+PV, useful when pressure is controlled and for steady-flow energy accounting; ΔH=Q_p only under suitable conditions.

cards.front: Define Helmholtz free energy in the context of Thermodynamics.
cards.back: F=U−TS; at fixed T,V,N a closed system tends toward lower F until equilibrium under the allowed processes.

cards.front: Define Gibbs free energy in the context of Thermodynamics.
cards.back: G=H−TS; at fixed T,P,N with only appropriate work modes, equilibrium minimizes G.

cards.front: Define Chemical potential in the context of Thermodynamics.
cards.back: Partial molar Gibbs free energy μ_i=(∂G/∂N_i)_{T,P,N_j}; it controls matter transfer and phase/reaction equilibrium.

cards.front: Define Heat capacity in the context of Thermodynamics.
cards.back: Energy/enthalpy response to temperature under specified constraints, e.g. C_V=(∂U/∂T)_V and C_P=(∂H/∂T)_P.

cards.front: Define Latent heat in the context of Thermodynamics.
cards.back: Heat transferred reversibly per amount during first-order phase change at coexistence temperature/pressure, associated with entropy discontinuity.

cards.front: Define Order parameter in the context of Thermodynamics.
cards.back: A quantity distinguishing phases, often tied to symmetry; its behavior depends on transition class.

cards.front: Define Coefficient of performance in the context of Thermodynamics.
cards.back: Desired heat transfer divided by work input for a refrigerator or heat pump; it can exceed one without violating energy conservation.

cards.front: Define Lumped-circuit approximation in the context of Basic Electronics and Instrumentation.
cards.back: Voltages/currents are treated as element variables and propagation delay across the circuit is negligible relative to signal timescale.

cards.front: Define Bias point in the context of Basic Electronics and Instrumentation.
cards.back: DC operating condition around which a nonlinear device can be linearized for a stated small-signal range.

cards.front: Define Impedance in the context of Basic Electronics and Instrumentation.
cards.back: Frequency-domain voltage-to-current ratio for a linear time-invariant element/network under sinusoidal steady state.

cards.front: Define Transfer function in the context of Basic Electronics and Instrumentation.
cards.back: Output/input transform ratio with zero initial conditions for a linear time-invariant model; poles and zeros govern dynamics.

cards.front: Define Negative feedback in the context of Basic Electronics and Instrumentation.
cards.back: A portion of output is returned to oppose input error, trading gain for controlled response, bandwidth/linearity, and potentially stability.

cards.front: Define Common-mode signal in the context of Basic Electronics and Instrumentation.
cards.back: Component shared by both inputs of a differential amplifier; finite rejection converts some into output error.

cards.front: Define Gain-bandwidth product in the context of Basic Electronics and Instrumentation.
cards.back: Approximate constant linking closed-loop gain and bandwidth for a dominant-pole op-amp in its valid regime.

cards.front: Define Slew rate in the context of Basic Electronics and Instrumentation.
cards.back: Maximum large-signal output voltage-change rate, distinct from small-signal bandwidth.

cards.front: Define Aliasing in the context of Basic Electronics and Instrumentation.
cards.back: Indistinguishable mapping of frequency components into sampled baseband because sampling is insufficient or input is not band-limited.

cards.front: Define Quantization in the context of Basic Electronics and Instrumentation.
cards.back: Mapping a continuous amplitude to discrete codes; error/noise depends on converter architecture, range, signal, and assumptions.

cards.front: Define Dynamic range in the context of Basic Electronics and Instrumentation.
cards.back: Ratio between largest usable signal and smallest resolvable/detectable signal under stated bandwidth, distortion, and error criteria.

cards.front: Define Sensitivity in the context of Basic Electronics and Instrumentation.
cards.back: Change in output per change in measurand, including units and operating point.

cards.front: Define Linearity in the context of Basic Electronics and Instrumentation.
cards.back: Closeness of response to a specified straight-line model over a declared range and calibration convention.

cards.front: Define Hysteresis in the context of Basic Electronics and Instrumentation.
cards.back: Different output for the same input depending on input history/direction.

cards.front: Define Ground in the context of Basic Electronics and Instrumentation.
cards.back: Chosen reference/return network; real grounds have impedance and can carry noise or fault current, so ground is not automatically zero everywhere.

cards.front: Define Dimension in the context of Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty.
cards.back: Physical type such as mass, length, time, current, or temperature, independent of unit choice.

cards.front: Define Unit in the context of Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty.
cards.back: Agreed magnitude used to express a quantity, such as metre or electronvolt; units can change while dimensions do not.

cards.front: Define Scalar and vector in the context of Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty.
cards.back: A scalar is invariant under coordinate rotations; a vector has magnitude/direction and transforms according to the vector rule.

cards.front: Define Gradient in the context of Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty.
cards.back: Vector of steepest local increase of a scalar field; directional derivative along unit u is u·∇f.

cards.front: Define Divergence in the context of Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty.
cards.back: Local net outward flux density of a vector field.

cards.front: Define Curl in the context of Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty.
cards.back: Local circulation/rotation density of a vector field, with orientation by right-hand rule.

cards.front: Define Eigenvector/eigenvalue in the context of Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty.
cards.back: Nonzero v satisfying Av=λv; transformation preserves its direction up to scaling λ.

cards.front: Define Condition number in the context of Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty.
cards.back: Measure of sensitivity of a problem/solution to perturbations under stated norm; large condition number can amplify data error.

cards.front: Define Boundary condition in the context of Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty.
cards.back: Constraint on solution at spatial boundary; different physical boundaries select different solutions/modes.

cards.front: Define Fourier transform in the context of Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty.
cards.back: Representation of a function in spatial/temporal frequency components under a stated convention.

cards.front: Define Random uncertainty in the context of Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty.
cards.back: Variation that changes unpredictably across repeated observations under repeatability conditions.

cards.front: Define Systematic effect in the context of Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty.
cards.back: Recognizable effect that shifts results through calibration, method, environment, model, or selection; repeats alone need not reveal/remove it.

cards.front: Define Covariance in the context of Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty.
cards.back: Joint variation measure Cov(X,Y)=E[(X−μ_X)(Y−μ_Y)]; it controls correlated uncertainty propagation.

cards.front: Define Likelihood in the context of Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty.
cards.back: Probability model for observed data as a function of model parameters; it is not the probability that a parameter is true.

cards.front: Define Residual in the context of Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty.
cards.back: Observed minus model-predicted value under a sign convention; residual structure diagnoses missing model behavior, dependence, or variance assumptions.

cards.front: Define Inertial frame in the context of Classical Mechanics and Oscillations.
cards.back: A frame in which a free particle moves with constant velocity and Newton’s second law holds without inertial-force corrections.

cards.front: Define Constraint in the context of Classical Mechanics and Oscillations.
cards.back: Restriction on allowed configurations or velocities; holonomic constraints can be written as relations among coordinates and time.

cards.front: Define Generalized coordinate in the context of Classical Mechanics and Oscillations.
cards.back: Independent parameter describing configuration after constraints, not necessarily a Cartesian length.

cards.front: Define Work in the context of Classical Mechanics and Oscillations.
cards.back: Line integral of force along displacement in the chosen frame; only the component along displacement contributes.

cards.front: Define Conservative force in the context of Classical Mechanics and Oscillations.
cards.back: Force derivable from a single-valued potential over the relevant domain, with path-independent work under stated conditions.

cards.front: Define Centre of mass in the context of Classical Mechanics and Oscillations.
cards.back: Mass-weighted position R=(Σm_i r_i)/M; its acceleration is set by net external force.

cards.front: Define Angular momentum in the context of Classical Mechanics and Oscillations.
cards.back: L=r×p about a specified origin; its time derivative equals torque with origin/frame qualifications.

cards.front: Define Coriolis force in the context of Classical Mechanics and Oscillations.
cards.back: In rotating coordinates, inertial force −2mΩ×v_rot acting on motion relative to the rotating frame.

cards.front: Define Lagrangian in the context of Classical Mechanics and Oscillations.
cards.back: Function L(q,q̇,t), often T−V, whose stationary action yields equations of motion for an appropriate model.

cards.front: Define Cyclic coordinate in the context of Classical Mechanics and Oscillations.
cards.back: Generalized coordinate absent explicitly from L; its conjugate momentum is conserved.

cards.front: Define Hamiltonian in the context of Classical Mechanics and Oscillations.
cards.back: Legendre transform H=Σp_iq̇_i−L when transformation is regular; generator of canonical time evolution.

cards.front: Define Phase space in the context of Classical Mechanics and Oscillations.
cards.back: Space of generalized coordinates and conjugate momenta; one system state is a point in it.

cards.front: Define Stable equilibrium in the context of Classical Mechanics and Oscillations.
cards.back: Equilibrium for which sufficiently small perturbations remain bounded; positive quadratic potential curvature is a local one-dimensional criterion.

cards.front: Define Normal mode in the context of Classical Mechanics and Oscillations.
cards.back: Collective oscillation pattern in which all coordinates vary at one eigenfrequency with fixed amplitude ratios.

cards.front: Define Dispersion in the context of Classical Mechanics and Oscillations.
cards.back: Dependence of angular frequency on wavevector; it separates phase and group velocities and can reshape pulses.

cards.front: Define Electric field E in the context of Electromagnetic Theory.
cards.back: Force per unit test charge in the limiting sense, including electric part of Lorentz force; units V/m or N/C.

cards.front: Define Electric potential V in the context of Electromagnetic Theory.
cards.back: Scalar whose electrostatic difference gives work per charge and E=−∇V in curl-free regions; reference is arbitrary.

cards.front: Define Electric displacement D in the context of Electromagnetic Theory.
cards.back: Auxiliary field with ∇·D=ρ_free under the chosen macroscopic split; D=ε₀E+P.

cards.front: Define Polarization P in the context of Electromagnetic Theory.
cards.back: Electric dipole moment per unit volume; spatial variation creates bound charge.

cards.front: Define Magnetic flux density B in the context of Electromagnetic Theory.
cards.back: Field entering magnetic Lorentz force qv×B and Faraday flux; units tesla.

cards.front: Define Magnetic field H in the context of Electromagnetic Theory.
cards.back: Auxiliary macroscopic field H=B/μ₀−M with curl tied to free current plus displacement term.

cards.front: Define Magnetization M in the context of Electromagnetic Theory.
cards.back: Magnetic dipole moment per unit volume; can be represented by bound currents under macroscopic model.

cards.front: Define Gauge freedom in the context of Electromagnetic Theory.
cards.back: Potentials can change by transformations leaving E and B unchanged; potentials are not unique.

cards.front: Define Displacement current in the context of Electromagnetic Theory.
cards.back: ε₀∂E/∂t in vacuum form, or ∂D/∂t in macroscopic Ampère–Maxwell law; it is a field term, not necessarily material charge crossing a gap.

cards.front: Define Poynting vector in the context of Electromagnetic Theory.
cards.back: S=E×H, electromagnetic energy-flux density in common macroscopic formulation.

cards.front: Define Wave impedance in the context of Electromagnetic Theory.
cards.back: Ratio of transverse electric to magnetic field amplitudes for a specified mode/medium, complex in lossy media.

cards.front: Define Skin depth in the context of Electromagnetic Theory.
cards.back: Distance over which field amplitude falls by e in a good conductor under harmonic steady state.

cards.front: Define Polarization of a wave in the context of Electromagnetic Theory.
cards.back: State of transverse electric-field orientation/evolution; distinct from material polarization P.

cards.front: Define Radiation pattern in the context of Electromagnetic Theory.
cards.back: Angular distribution of radiated power/intensity in a stated far-field plane or solid angle.

cards.front: Define Near and far field in the context of Electromagnetic Theory.
cards.back: Regions where reactive/source-size terms dominate versus radiative angular field with approximately transverse 1/r behavior; boundary depends on wavelength and aperture size.

cards.front: Define Quantum state in the context of Quantum Mechanics.
cards.back: A ray in Hilbert space representing a preparation; normalized vectors differing only by global phase represent the same pure state.

cards.front: Define Wavefunction in the context of Quantum Mechanics.
cards.back: State amplitude in a chosen basis, e.g. ψ(x)=⟨x|ψ⟩; it is not directly a classical material wave.

cards.front: Define Born rule in the context of Quantum Mechanics.
cards.back: Probability density for position is |ψ(x)|², and more generally outcome probability is given by projection/POVM rule.

cards.front: Define Observable in the context of Quantum Mechanics.
cards.back: Physical quantity represented ideally by a self-adjoint operator or more generally a measurement operator framework.

cards.front: Define Expectation value in the context of Quantum Mechanics.
cards.back: Ensemble mean predicted for repeated identically prepared measurements, ⟨A⟩=⟨ψ|A|ψ⟩.

cards.front: Define Commutator in the context of Quantum Mechanics.
cards.back: [A,B]=AB−BA; it encodes compatibility, dynamics and uncertainty relations.

cards.front: Define Stationary state in the context of Quantum Mechanics.
cards.back: Energy eigenstate whose time evolution is a phase e^(−iEt/ħ), leaving time-independent expectation of time-independent observables.

cards.front: Define Degeneracy in the context of Quantum Mechanics.
cards.back: Two or more independent states share an eigenvalue, often due to symmetry.

cards.front: Define Parity in the context of Quantum Mechanics.
cards.back: Spatial inversion symmetry; in one dimension parity eigenvalues are ±1 for symmetric potentials.

cards.front: Define Probability current in the context of Quantum Mechanics.
cards.back: j=(ħ/m)Im(ψ*∇ψ) for the standard Schrödinger particle; with density it satisfies continuity.

cards.front: Define Tunnelling in the context of Quantum Mechanics.
cards.back: Nonzero transmission/amplitude through a region classically forbidden at the same total energy.

cards.front: Define Spin in the context of Quantum Mechanics.
cards.back: Intrinsic angular momentum with no classical rigid-body interpretation; spin-½ has two outcomes along any axis.

cards.front: Define Identical particles in the context of Quantum Mechanics.
cards.back: Particles of same species whose labels are not physical observables; many-body state is symmetric for bosons and antisymmetric for fermions.

cards.front: Define Perturbation theory in the context of Quantum Mechanics.
cards.back: Controlled expansion around a solvable Hamiltonian when perturbation is sufficiently small relative to relevant gaps/matrix elements.

cards.front: Define Variational principle in the context of Quantum Mechanics.
cards.back: For normalized trial state, expectation of H is at least ground-state energy; quality depends on trial family.

cards.front: Define Microstate in the context of Statistical Mechanics.
cards.back: Complete microscopic specification compatible with the model, e.g. phase-space point or quantum many-body state.

cards.front: Define Macrostate in the context of Statistical Mechanics.
cards.back: Specification by coarse thermodynamic variables such as E,V,N,T,P; many microstates can share it.

cards.front: Define Multiplicity Ω in the context of Statistical Mechanics.
cards.back: Number or measure of accessible microstates under stated constraints and coarse graining.

cards.front: Define Ensemble in the context of Statistical Mechanics.
cards.back: Probability distribution over hypothetical copies/microstates representing preparation constraints.

cards.front: Define Microcanonical ensemble in the context of Statistical Mechanics.
cards.back: Isolated equilibrium ensemble with fixed E,V,N within a narrow energy shell and equal a priori probabilities under assumptions.

cards.front: Define Canonical ensemble in the context of Statistical Mechanics.
cards.back: Subsystem at fixed T,V,N exchanging energy weakly with a large bath; p_i=e^(−βE_i)/Z.

cards.front: Define Grand canonical ensemble in the context of Statistical Mechanics.
cards.back: Subsystem at fixed T,V,μ exchanging energy and particles; weights e^{−β(E−μN)}.

cards.front: Define Partition function in the context of Statistical Mechanics.
cards.back: Sum/integral of Boltzmann weights over states for an ensemble; normalization and thermodynamic generator.

cards.front: Define Density of states in the context of Statistical Mechanics.
cards.back: Number of available states per energy interval (and often per volume), including degeneracy conventions.

cards.front: Define Thermodynamic limit in the context of Statistical Mechanics.
cards.back: N,V→∞ with densities fixed, where surface/relative fluctuations often vanish and ensemble equivalence may emerge away from singularities.

cards.front: Define Equipartition in the context of Statistical Mechanics.
cards.back: Each independent quadratic term in a classical Hamiltonian contributes ½k_BT to mean energy under canonical assumptions.

cards.front: Define Chemical potential in the context of Statistical Mechanics.
cards.back: Thermodynamic cost of adding a particle; controls equilibrium occupation and exchange.

cards.front: Define Degenerate quantum gas in the context of Statistical Mechanics.
cards.back: Regime where wavefunction overlap/quantum statistics dominate, often nλ_th³ not small.

cards.front: Define Fluctuation in the context of Statistical Mechanics.
cards.back: Spontaneous variation of a microscopic/mesoscopic observable around equilibrium ensemble mean.

cards.front: Define Ergodic hypothesis in the context of Statistical Mechanics.
cards.back: Under suitable dynamics, long-time averages equal ensemble averages for relevant observables; not universally guaranteed.

cards.front: Define Isotope in the context of Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection.
cards.back: Nuclei with same proton number Z and different neutron number N.

cards.front: Define Isotone and isobar in the context of Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection.
cards.back: Isotones share N; isobars share mass number A=N+Z.

cards.front: Define Binding energy in the context of Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection.
cards.back: Energy required to separate nucleus into free nucleons, equal to mass defect times c² under consistent masses.

cards.front: Define Nuclear force in the context of Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection.
cards.back: Effective short-range nucleon interaction with spin/isospin dependence and saturation; not a simple inverse-square force.

cards.front: Define Magic number in the context of Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection.
cards.back: Nucleon count associated with closed shell and enhanced stability patterns in shell model.

cards.front: Define Activity in the context of Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection.
cards.back: Expected decay rate A=λN, measured in becquerel (s⁻¹).

cards.front: Define Half-life and mean life in the context of Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection.
cards.back: T₁/₂=ln2/λ; τ=1/λ for exponential decay.

cards.front: Define Q value in the context of Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection.
cards.back: Initial rest energy minus final rest energy using consistent masses; positive Q means energy release in centre-of-mass accounting.

cards.front: Define Cross section in the context of Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection.
cards.back: Interaction-rate measure with area units; reaction rate depends on flux, target number and cross section.

cards.front: Define Criticality in the context of Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection.
cards.back: For a multiplying neutron system, k_eff=1 means one generation sustains the next on average; it is not synonymous with accident.

cards.front: Define Absorbed dose in the context of Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection.
cards.back: Energy imparted by ionizing radiation per unit mass, measured in gray (J/kg).

cards.front: Define Equivalent dose in the context of Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection.
cards.back: Absorbed dose to tissue weighted by radiation type, measured in sievert.

cards.front: Define Effective dose in the context of Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection.
cards.back: Equivalent doses additionally weighted by tissue sensitivity for protection/risk comparison; not an individual deterministic outcome.

cards.front: Define Irradiation versus contamination in the context of Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection.
cards.back: Irradiation is exposure to a radiation field; contamination means radioactive material is present on a surface, body or internally.

cards.front: Define ALARA in the context of Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection.
cards.back: Optimization principle to keep exposures as low as reasonably achievable within justified, regulated practice—not a numerical formula.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: Define Specific orbital energy in the context of Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing.
cards.back: Mechanical orbital energy per unit mass ε=v²/2−μ/r in two-body model.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: Define Specific angular momentum in the context of Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing.
cards.back: h=r×v per unit mass; constant vector for ideal central gravity and fixes orbital plane.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: Define Orbital elements in the context of Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing.
cards.back: Six parameters specifying ideal conic size/shape/orientation and location; conventions/singularities require care.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: Define Periapsis and apoapsis in the context of Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing.
cards.back: Nearest and farthest orbital radii from focus; Earth-specific names perigee/apogee.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: Define Geostationary orbit in the context of Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing.
cards.back: Ideal circular, equatorial, prograde orbit with sidereal-day period, appearing fixed over one longitude.

cards.front: Define Sun-synchronous orbit in the context of Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing.

cards.back: Ability to distinguish signal-level/radiance differences, affected by noise, calibration, bit depth and dynamic range.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: Define Ground truth in the context of Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing.
cards.back: Independent in-situ/reference observations matched in space/time/scale to validate/calibrate remote-sensing products.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Bragg condition (Solid State Physics).
cards.back: nλ = 2dₕₖₗ sin θ — Constructive interference occurs when path difference between waves from adjacent planes is an integer wavelength. Units: λ and d in the same length unit; n and sinθ dimensionless Conditions: Elastic, approximately monochromatic scattering from a periodic set of planes; measured diffractometer angle is commonly 2θ.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Reciprocal basis (Solid State Physics).
cards.back: b₁ = 2π(a₂×a₃)/[a₁·(a₂×a₃)] and cyclic permutations — aᵢ·bⱼ=2πδᵢⱼ makes plane waves compatible with lattice translations. Units: bᵢ has m⁻¹ if aᵢ has m Conditions: Primitive vectors must be linearly independent.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Cubic plane spacing (Solid State Physics).
cards.back: dₕₖₗ = a/√(h²+k²+l²) — Higher-index cubic planes generally have smaller spacing. Units: d and a are lengths Conditions: Valid for cubic metric only; other crystal systems require the appropriate metric tensor.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Drude conductivity (Solid State Physics).
cards.back: σ = nq²τ/m* — Conductivity grows with carrier density and relaxation time and falls with inertial response. Units: σ in S·m⁻¹ Conditions: Single-carrier, semiclassical, linear-response relaxation-time model.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Hall coefficient (Solid State Physics).
cards.back: R_H = 1/(nq) and V_H = R_H I B/t — Hall sign identifies dominant carrier sign in a simple model; magnitude estimates density. Units: R_H in m³·C⁻¹; V_H in V Conditions: Single dominant carrier, homogeneous geometry, linear field response; mobility additionally needs σ or ρ.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Mobility relation (Solid State Physics).
cards.back: σ = n|q|μ — Mobility connects drift velocity to electric field and combines transport scattering with effective mass. Units: μ in m²·V⁻¹·s⁻¹ Conditions: Use only with a carrier model consistent with Hall and conductivity measurements.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Fermi–Dirac occupation (Solid State Physics).
cards.back: f(E)=1/{exp[(E−μ)/(k_BT)]+1} — Probability that a fermion state of energy E is occupied in equilibrium. Units: f dimensionless Conditions: Thermal equilibrium and noninteracting quasiparticle description for the stated states.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Free-electron Fermi energy (Solid State Physics).
cards.back: E_F = (ħ²/2m)(3π²n)^(2/3) — At zero temperature, states fill up to E_F in a three-dimensional spin-½ free-electron gas. Units: E_F in J or eV Conditions: Three-dimensional, noninteracting, parabolic dispersion, two spin states.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Scherrer estimate (Solid State Physics).
cards.back: D = Kλ/(β cosθ) — Finite coherent size broadens diffraction peaks. Units: D and λ same length unit Conditions: β must be corrected for instrumental broadening; strain, defects, overlap, and line-shape choice can invalidate a size-only interpretation. D is not particle size.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Bragg condition (Materials Characterization).
cards.back: nλ=2d sinθ — Relates a diffraction maximum to periodic plane spacing. Units: λ,d length Conditions: Elastic scattering, known wavelength, indexed geometry; position alone does not establish purity.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Beer–Lambert attenuation (Materials Characterization).
cards.back: I=I₀e^(−αx), A=−log₁₀T — Ideal exponential attenuation for independent absorbers or a homogeneous effective medium. Units: α inverse length; A,T dimensionless Conditions: Requires suitable baseline, path length, low multiple scattering, detector linearity, and a justified use of absorbance.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Raman shift (Materials Characterization).
cards.back: Δν̃=(1/λ₀−1/λ_s) with wavelengths in cm — Reports photon wavenumber change associated with sample excitations. Units: Δν̃ in cm⁻¹ Conditions: Calibrate spectral axis; account for fluorescence, heating, resolution, and Stokes/anti-Stokes sign convention.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify XPS binding energy (Materials Characterization).
cards.back: E_B=hν−E_K−Φ_spec — Photoelectron energy conservation supports elemental and chemical-state analysis. Units: Energy, commonly eV Conditions: Requires energy calibration/charge referencing and surface-sensitive interpretation.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Scherrer estimate (Materials Characterization).
cards.back: D=Kλ/(β cosθ) — Finite coherent-domain size can broaden diffraction peaks. Units: D,λ length Conditions: Instrument correction and separation from strain/defect/overlap effects are essential.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Single-carrier Hall (Materials Characterization).
cards.back: R_H=1/(nq), μ=|R_H|σ — Combines transverse and longitudinal transport under a one-carrier model. Units: R_H m³/C; μ m²/(V·s) Conditions: Homogeneous geometry, correct thickness, linear field, one dominant carrier; not generally valid for multiband transport.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Thin-film sheet resistance (Materials Characterization).
cards.back: R_s=(π/ln2)(V/I)F for an ideal collinear four-probe geometry — Converts measured V/I to sheet resistance for the stated probe/sample geometry. Units: R_s in Ω per square Conditions: Probe spacing, thickness, boundaries, contact placement, and heating determine F.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Independent uncertainty propagation (Materials Characterization).
cards.back: u_y²≈Σ(∂f/∂xᵢ)²uᵢ² — First-order propagation of small independent input uncertainties. Units: u_y has units of y Conditions: Include covariance terms for correlated inputs; nonlinear/asymmetric cases may need simulation or full propagation.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Signal-to-noise ratio (Materials Characterization).
cards.back: SNR=signal measure/noise measure — Compares signal scale with noise under a declared convention. Units: Dimensionless, sometimes reported in dB Conditions: Never quote SNR without defining bandwidth, baseline, statistic, and processing.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Snell’s law (Optics and Lasers).
cards.back: n₁ sinθ₁=n₂ sinθ₂ — Tangential wavevector/phase matching across a planar interface. Units: Dimensionless Conditions: Homogeneous isotropic media, defined frequency; complex/anisotropic media require a fuller treatment.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Thin-lens equation (Optics and Lasers).
cards.back: 1/f=1/s+1/s′ — Connects conjugate planes for a paraxial thin lens. Units: All lengths in one unit Conditions: Real-is-positive convention stated here; thin lens, paraxial rays, same refractive medium on both sides. Other sign conventions change algebraic signs.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Phase from optical path (Optics and Lasers).
cards.back: Δφ=(2π/λ₀)Δ(OPL) — Converts optical-path difference into monochromatic phase difference. Units: Phase in radians Conditions: Use phase index at the frequency and include reflection phase shifts where relevant.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Two-beam interference (Optics and Lasers).
cards.back: I=I₁+I₂+2√(I₁I₂)|γ₁₂|cos(Δφ+argγ₁₂) — Visibility depends on amplitude balance and mutual coherence. Units: I in W/m² or consistent detector units Conditions: Same polarization component and detector averaging; for perfect coherence |γ|=1.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Single-slit Fraunhofer pattern (Optics and Lasers).
cards.back: I(θ)=I₀(sinβ/β)², β=πa sinθ/λ — Finite aperture produces a sinc-squared angular intensity envelope. Units: β dimensionless Conditions: Uniform slit illumination, scalar far-field diffraction; minima a sinθ=mλ for nonzero integer m.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Grating equation (Optics and Lasers).
cards.back: d(sinθ_m−sinθ_i)=mλ — Periodic aperture gives discrete diffraction orders. Units: d,λ length Conditions: Angle signs must follow one convention; at normal incidence it reduces to d sinθ_m=mλ.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Rayleigh circular-aperture criterion (Optics and Lasers).
cards.back: θ_R≈1.22λ/D — A conventional diffraction-limited angular-separation criterion. Units: θ in radians Conditions: Uniform circular aperture, incoherent point sources, far field; it is a criterion, not a universal information limit.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Malus’s law (Optics and Lasers).
cards.back: I=I₀ cos²θ — Projection of field gives cosine amplitude and cosine-squared intensity. Units: Intensity/power units Conditions: Incident light linearly polarized, ideal analyzer; use Stokes/Jones treatment for general states/elements.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Brewster angle (Optics and Lasers).
cards.back: tanθ_B=n₂/n₁ — Reflected p-polarized amplitude vanishes in the ideal Fresnel model. Units: Dimensionless Conditions: Planar interface, real indices; absorption, roughness, anisotropy, or magnetic response modify the result.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Wave-plate retardance (Optics and Lasers).
cards.back: δ=(2π/λ₀)Δn L — Orthogonal eigenpolarizations accumulate different phase. Units: δ radians Conditions: Uniform plate, known wavelength, propagation along stated direction; dispersion and multiple reflections can matter.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Laser threshold (Optics and Lasers).
cards.back: g_th=α_i+(1/2L)ln[1/(R₁R₂)] — Round-trip gain balances distributed and mirror losses. Units: g,α_i inverse length Conditions: Steady single-pass gain model, uniform gain/loss, no saturation or spatial-hole-burning corrections.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Ideal photodiode responsivity (Optics and Lasers).
cards.back: ℛ=ηq/(hν)=ηqλ/(hc) — Each collected carrier per photon converts photon flux to current. Units: A/W Conditions: One collected electron charge per detected photon and linear unsaturated operation; real η and gain depend on device.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify First law, closed system (Thermodynamics).
cards.back: dU=δQ−δW_by — Energy conservation under the declared sign convention. Units: J Conditions: Include all relevant work modes; for quasistatic PV work δW_by=P_ext dV, equal to P dV only in reversible mechanical equilibrium.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Fundamental relation (Thermodynamics).
cards.back: dU=T dS−P dV+Σμ_i dN_i — Defines intensive conjugates for a simple multicomponent compressible system. Units: Every term J Conditions: Equilibrium fundamental equation; add other generalized work terms when present.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Ideal-gas equation (Thermodynamics).
cards.back: PV=nRT=Nk_BT — Equation of state for an ideal gas. Units: P Pa, V m³, T K Conditions: Negligible interaction volume/forces in the regime; not a universal gas law.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Enthalpy differential (Thermodynamics).
cards.back: dH=T dS+V dP+Σμ_i dN_i — Natural variables S,P,N. Units: J Conditions: Simple compressible system with composition terms as shown.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Helmholtz differential (Thermodynamics).
cards.back: dF=−S dT−P dV+Σμ_i dN_i — Generates S=−(∂F/∂T)_V and P=−(∂F/∂V)_T. Units: J Conditions: Equilibrium simple system.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Gibbs differential (Thermodynamics).
cards.back: dG=−S dT+V dP+Σμ_i dN_i — Generates entropy, volume, and chemical potentials under T,P control. Units: J Conditions: Equilibrium simple system; constraints matter for minimum principle.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Entropy balance (Thermodynamics).
cards.back: ΔS_system=∫δQ/T_boundary+S_gen, with S_gen≥0 — Separates entropy transfer from internal production. Units: J/K Conditions: Use appropriate boundary temperatures and matter-flow terms for open systems.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Ideal-gas heat capacities (Thermodynamics).
cards.back: C_P−C_V=nR (total) or C̄_P−C̄_V=R (molar) — Mayer relation for an ideal gas. Units: J/K total or J/(mol·K) molar Conditions: Ideal gas; heat capacities may depend on temperature.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Reversible adiabatic ideal gas (Thermodynamics).
cards.back: PV^γ=const, TV^(γ−1)=const — Combines first law and ideal-gas equation for isentropic path. Units: Constants carry corresponding units Conditions: Ideal gas, constant heat capacities for simple power law, reversible and adiabatic—not merely adiabatic.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Carnot limits (Thermodynamics).
cards.back: η_C=1−T_C/T_H; COP_R=T_C/(T_H−T_C) — Maximum reversible engine efficiency and refrigerator COP between two reservoirs. Units: Dimensionless Conditions: Reversible cyclic device; real performance is lower.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Clausius–Clapeyron (Thermodynamics).
cards.back: dP_sat/dT≈L P_sat/(R T²), ln(P₂/P₁)=−L/R(1/T₂−1/T₁) — Approximate vapor-pressure variation when vapor ideal and condensed volume negligible. Units: Slope Pa/K Conditions: L approximately constant over interval; general Clapeyron is dP/dT=ΔS/ΔV=ΔH/(TΔV).

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify One Maxwell relation (Thermodynamics).
cards.back: (∂S/∂V)_T=(∂P/∂T)_V — Relates difficult entropy derivative to measurable equation-of-state response. Units: Both Pa/K = J/(m³K) Conditions: F twice differentiable and equilibrium variables well behaved away from singularities.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Ohm and power (Basic Electronics and Instrumentation).
cards.back: V=IR; P=VI=I²R=V²/R — Linear resistor and electrical power relations. Units: V, A, Ω, W Conditions: Ohmic constant R over operating range; temperature and self-heating may change R.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Capacitor and inductor (Basic Electronics and Instrumentation).
cards.back: i_C=C dv/dt; v_L=L di/dt — Energy-storage elements resist instantaneous voltage/current changes respectively. Units: F and H Conditions: Ideal lumped elements; parasitics and saturation omitted.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Impedances (Basic Electronics and Instrumentation).
cards.back: Z_R=R; Z_C=1/(jωC); Z_L=jωL — Sinusoidal steady-state element response. Units: Ω Conditions: Linear time-invariant lumped model; initial transients excluded.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify RC time constant (Basic Electronics and Instrumentation).
cards.back: τ=RC; v_C(t)=V_f+(V_0−V_f)e^(−t/RC) — First-order exponential response. Units: τ seconds Conditions: Thevenin resistance seen by capacitor constant and independent sources stepped.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Diode equation (Basic Electronics and Instrumentation).
cards.back: I=I_S[exp(V_D/(nV_T))−1], V_T=k_BT/q — Idealized junction current-voltage relation. Units: I A, V V Conditions: Specified temperature and regime; series resistance, breakdown, high injection, leakage and recombination require corrections.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Op-amp feedback gains (Basic Electronics and Instrumentation).
cards.back: Inverting: V_o/V_i=−R_f/R_in; non-inverting: 1+R_f/R_g — Ideal negative-feedback gains from virtual-short/current assumptions. Units: Dimensionless Conditions: Stable negative feedback, unsaturated output, input common-mode/output swing/bandwidth limits satisfied, input currents negligible.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Feedback closed-loop gain (Basic Electronics and Instrumentation).
cards.back: A_cl=A/(1+Aβ) — Large loop gain makes closed-loop response approach 1/β and reduces sensitivity to A. Units: Dimensionless Conditions: Scalar linear model with negative-feedback sign; stability requires loop phase/magnitude analysis.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify First-order low-pass (Basic Electronics and Instrumentation).
cards.back: H(jω)=1/(1+jωRC); f_c=1/(2πRC) — Passes low frequencies and attenuates high frequencies with one pole. Units: f Hz Conditions: Ideal source/load assumptions or use actual Thevenin/load resistance.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Sampling condition (Basic Electronics and Instrumentation).
cards.back: f_s>2B — Uniform samples can represent/reconstruct an ideal band-limited signal under the sampling theorem. Units: Hz Conditions: Practical systems need anti-alias filtering and transition margin; equality is not robust.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Ideal ADC step (Basic Electronics and Instrumentation).
cards.back: LSB≈V_FS/2^N — Nominal code width for an ideal uniform converter. Units: V/code Conditions: Endpoint convention, offset/gain error, DNL/INL, reference, noise and effective number of bits matter.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Johnson noise (Basic Electronics and Instrumentation).
cards.back: v_n,rms=√(4k_BTRB) — Thermal voltage noise of a resistor in classical white-noise regime. Units: V rms Conditions: Matched measurement model, stated bandwidth and temperature; quantum/high-frequency corrections may apply.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Shot noise (Basic Electronics and Instrumentation).
cards.back: i_n,rms=√(2qIB) — Poisson arrival noise for independent charge carriers. Units: A rms Conditions: Full shot-noise assumption; correlations, device gain/excess noise and filtering modify it.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Calibration line (Basic Electronics and Instrumentation).
cards.back: y=a+bx; u_x includes fit, reference, repeatability and model terms — Maps sensor output to measurand. Units: b has output/input units Conditions: Use only over validated range; inspect residuals, hysteresis, drift, covariance and extrapolation.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Dimensional homogeneity (Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty).
cards.back: [left side]=[right side] — Every additive term in a physical equation must share dimensions. Units: Dimension equation Conditions: Necessary but not sufficient for correctness; cannot determine dimensionless constants or full functional form.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Gauss divergence theorem (Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty).
cards.back: ∭_V ∇·F dV=∯_∂V F·n dA — Volume integral of sources equals outward boundary flux. Units: Both sides field×area Conditions: Field and region sufficiently regular; singularities require distribution/exclusion treatment.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Stokes theorem (Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty).
cards.back: ∬_S (∇×F)·n dA=∮_∂S F·dl — Surface-integrated curl equals boundary circulation. Units: Both sides field×length Conditions: Smooth oriented surface/field with compatible boundary orientation.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Linear eigenproblem (Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty).
cards.back: Av=λv; det(A−λI)=0 — Natural modes diagonalize a linear transformation when a complete basis exists. Units: λ carries A’s units Conditions: Not every matrix is diagonalizable; Hermitian matrices have orthonormal eigenbasis in finite dimensions.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify First-order decay/growth ODE (Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty).
cards.back: dy/dt=−ky ⇒ y=y₀e^(−kt) — Constant fractional rate gives exponential response. Units: Exponent dimensionless Conditions: k constant and model autonomous/linear over regime.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Fourier transform pair (Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty).
cards.back: F(k)=∫f(x)e^(−ikx)dx; f(x)=(1/2π)∫F(k)e^(ikx)dk — Decomposes a function into wavenumber components. Units: F has f×x units under this convention Conditions: Function/distribution must permit transform; normalization conventions vary.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Mean, variance, covariance (Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty).
cards.back: μ=E[X]; σ²=E[(X−μ)²]; Cov(X,Y)=E[(X−μ_X)(Y−μ_Y)] — Location, spread, and joint variation. Units: Variance X², covariance XY Conditions: Moments must exist; sample estimators and denominator conventions differ.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Poisson distribution (Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty).
cards.back: P(N=k)=e^(−λ)λ^k/k!; E[N]=Var(N)=λ — Independent events at constant rate in fixed interval. Units: Counts dimensionless Conditions: Independence/stationary rate/no pile-up; background and dead time can violate model.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Gaussian density (Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty).
cards.back: p(x)=exp[−(x−μ)²/(2σ²)]/(σ√(2π)) — Continuous symmetric location-scale model. Units: p inverse units of x Conditions: Do not assume automatically; tails, mixtures, truncation and correlation matter.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify First-order uncertainty propagation (Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty).
cards.back: u_y²≈Σ_iΣ_j (∂f/∂x_i)(∂f/∂x_j)Cov(x_i,x_j) — Taylor-linearized propagation including correlations. Units: u_y same units as y Conditions: Small uncertainties and local linearity; use nonlinear/Monte Carlo treatment when needed.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Weighted mean (Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty).
cards.back: x̄_w=Σw_i x_i/Σw_i; w_i=1/u_i²; u(x̄_w)=1/√Σw_i — Inverse-variance weighting gives more weight to more precise independent estimates. Units: Same as x Conditions: Quoted u_i credible, no unmodelled correlation/heterogeneity; check consistency.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Ordinary least-squares line (Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty).
cards.back: b=Σ(x_i−x̄)(y_i−ȳ)/Σ(x_i−x̄)²; a=ȳ−b x̄ — Minimizes unweighted vertical squared residuals. Units: b y/x; a y Conditions: x treated known, independent equal-variance zero-mean residuals for standard inference; fitting does not establish causation.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Reduced chi-square (Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty).
cards.back: χ²_ν=Σ[(y_i−f_i)/u_i]²/(N−p) — Compares residual scale with stated independent Gaussian uncertainties. Units: Dimensionless Conditions: Interpret only with correct model, uncertainties, independence and degrees of freedom; near one is not proof of truth.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Standard error of mean (Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty).
cards.back: SE=s/√N — Uncertainty of sample mean from independent identically distributed finite-variance observations. Units: Same as measurand Conditions: Not total measurement uncertainty; correlation, drift and systematic effects invalidate simple scaling.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Newton’s second law (Classical Mechanics and Oscillations).
cards.back: ΣF_ext=dp/dt; for constant m, ΣF=ma — Net external force changes momentum in an inertial frame. Units: N=kg·m/s² Conditions: State system/frame; variable-mass systems require momentum-flux treatment rather than naive m dv/dt alone.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Work-energy theorem (Classical Mechanics and Oscillations).
cards.back: W_net=∫F_net·dr=ΔK — Net work changes kinetic energy. Units: J Conditions: Particle/inertial-frame form; include constraints, deformable bodies and frame choice appropriately.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Linear momentum balance (Classical Mechanics and Oscillations).
cards.back: dP/dt=F_ext — Internal action-reaction forces cancel under the model, leaving external force for total momentum. Units: kg·m/s Conditions: Closed particle system with suitable internal-force symmetry; fields/flux may carry momentum.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Angular momentum balance (Classical Mechanics and Oscillations).
cards.back: dL_O/dt=τ_O,ext — External torque changes angular momentum. Units: kg·m²/s Conditions: Inertial origin or include moving-origin terms; define particle/body system.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Rigid-body rotation about fixed principal axis (Classical Mechanics and Oscillations).
cards.back: τ=Iα; K_rot=½Iω² — Rotational analog under fixed-axis assumptions. Units: I kg·m² Conditions: Rigid body and fixed principal axis; general rotation uses tensors and Euler equations.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Rotating-frame acceleration (Classical Mechanics and Oscillations).
cards.back: a_I=a_O+a_R+2Ω×v_R+Ω×(Ω×r)+Ω̇×r — Relates inertial acceleration to relative, Coriolis, centrifugal and Euler terms. Units: m/s² Conditions: r measured from moving origin; signs of fictitious forces are negative of extra acceleration terms in m a_R equation.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Euler–Lagrange equation (Classical Mechanics and Oscillations).
cards.back: d/dt(∂L/∂q̇_i)−∂L/∂q_i=0 — Stationary-action equations for independent variations. Units: Generalized force units Conditions: Appropriate L, ideal/handled constraints and fixed endpoint variations.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Hamilton equations (Classical Mechanics and Oscillations).
cards.back: q̇_i=∂H/∂p_i; ṗ_i=−∂H/∂q_i — First-order phase-space evolution. Units: Consistent canonical units Conditions: Regular Legendre transform; H need not equal energy for time-dependent coordinates/potentials.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Central-force effective potential (Classical Mechanics and Oscillations).
cards.back: E=½m ṙ²+V_eff(r); V_eff=V(r)+ℓ²/(2mr²) — Radial motion becomes one-dimensional with centrifugal barrier. Units: J Conditions: Time-independent central force, reduced one-body description and planar motion.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Small oscillation (Classical Mechanics and Oscillations).
cards.back: m ẍ+kx=0; ω₀=√(k/m) — Quadratic potential gives sinusoidal motion. Units: ω rad/s Conditions: Small displacement, linear restoring force, constant parameters, negligible damping/driving.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Damped oscillator (Classical Mechanics and Oscillations).
cards.back: m ẍ+b ẋ+kx=0; β=b/(2m); ω_d=√(ω₀²−β²) — Underdamped motion decays at rate β and oscillates at ω_d. Units: s⁻¹ Conditions: Linear viscous damping; underdamped when β<ω₀.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Driven response amplitude (Classical Mechanics and Oscillations).
cards.back: A(ω)=F₀/m /√[(ω₀²−ω²)²+(2βω)²] — Steady-state amplitude peaks near resonance with damping-dependent frequency/width. Units: m Conditions: Linear steady state after transient; displacement resonance is not exactly ω₀ when damping finite.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Quality factor (Classical Mechanics and Oscillations).
cards.back: Q≈ω₀/(2β)=mω₀/b — Measures stored energy relative to loss per radian/cycle convention and relates to resonance width. Units: Dimensionless Conditions: Linear weakly damped oscillator; define bandwidth/energy convention.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Phase and group velocities (Classical Mechanics and Oscillations).
cards.back: v_p=ω/k; v_g=dω/dk — Phase fronts and narrowband envelope propagate differently in dispersive media. Units: m/s Conditions: Group velocity envelope interpretation requires narrow bandwidth and care in loss/anomalous dispersion.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Coulomb field (Electromagnetic Theory).
cards.back: E(r)=q r̂/(4πε₀r²) — Inverse-square electrostatic field. Units: V/m Conditions: Point/static charge, vacuum, superposition; real distributions require integration and material boundaries.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Electrostatic potential (Electromagnetic Theory).
cards.back: E=−∇V; ∇²V=−ρ/ε₀ — Potential converts electrostatic field to scalar boundary-value problem. Units: V and V/m Conditions: Electrostatics; in charge-free region ∇²V=0.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Gauss laws (Electromagnetic Theory).
cards.back: ∇·E=ρ/ε₀; ∇·B=0 — Charge sources electric flux; no observed magnetic monopole source in Maxwell theory. Units: Consistent SI Conditions: Integral forms handle distributions/surfaces; macroscopic D uses free charge.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Lorentz force (Electromagnetic Theory).
cards.back: F=q(E+v×B) — Force on point charge from electromagnetic fields. Units: N Conditions: Classical point-particle form; radiation reaction/relativity and material forces may require extensions.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Biot–Savart law (Electromagnetic Theory).
cards.back: B(r)=μ₀/(4π)∫ I dℓ′×R̂/R² — Magnetostatic field from current element. Units: T Conditions: Steady localized current; full time-dependent fields require retarded solutions/Maxwell equations.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Faraday law (Electromagnetic Theory).
cards.back: ∇×E=−∂B/∂t; ∮E·dl=−dΦ_B/dt — Changing magnetic flux is linked to circulating electric field. Units: V/m curl Conditions: Moving/deforming circuits require motional EMF qv×B contribution and careful flux rule.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Ampère–Maxwell law (Electromagnetic Theory).
cards.back: ∇×B=μ₀J+μ₀ε₀∂E/∂t — Current and changing electric field source magnetic curl. Units: T/m Conditions: Macroscopic media commonly use ∇×H=J_free+∂D/∂t.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Vacuum wave equations (Electromagnetic Theory).
cards.back: ∇²E−(1/c²)∂²E/∂t²=0; same for B; c=1/√(μ₀ε₀) — Maxwell equations support transverse waves. Units: Each term field/m² Conditions: ρ=0, J=0, homogeneous vacuum; sources/boundaries add inhomogeneous terms.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Plane-wave relations (Electromagnetic Theory).
cards.back: B=(1/ω)k×E; |E|/|H|=Z₀=√(μ₀/ε₀) — E,B,k mutually perpendicular with fixed amplitude relation. Units: Z₀ Ω Conditions: Source-free vacuum plane wave; lossy/anisotropic/guided modes differ.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Poynting theorem (Electromagnetic Theory).
cards.back: ∂u/∂t+∇·S=−J·E; u=½(ε₀E²+B²/μ₀), S=E×H — Local electromagnetic energy conservation. Units: W/m³ balance Conditions: Material dispersion/loss requires careful energy definitions; J·E is power transferred to matter.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Boundary conditions (Electromagnetic Theory).
cards.back: n·(D₂−D₁)=σ_f; n×(E₂−E₁)=0; n·(B₂−B₁)=0; n×(H₂−H₁)=K_f — Normal/tangential jumps follow pillbox/loop Maxwell integrals. Units: Surface charge C/m²; current A/m Conditions: No impulsive time-varying surface flux for displayed E tangential form; orientations/signs stated.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Parallel-plate capacitance (Electromagnetic Theory).
cards.back: C≈εA/d; U=½CV²; u_E=½E·D — Geometry/material store electric energy. Units: F, J, J/m³ Conditions: Neglect fringing, linear nondispersive dielectric for simple energy density.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Good-conductor skin depth (Electromagnetic Theory).
cards.back: δ≈√[2/(ωμσ)] — Harmonic field amplitude decays over δ and phase advances similarly. Units: m Conditions: Good conductor σ≫ωε, homogeneous linear medium.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Friis free-space relation (Electromagnetic Theory).
cards.back: P_r=P_tG_tG_r(λ/4πR)² — Ideal free-space link scaling. Units: W Conditions: Line of sight, far field, no multipath/atmosphere/mismatch; gains and losses consistently defined.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Time-dependent Schrödinger equation (Quantum Mechanics).
cards.back: iħ∂|ψ⟩/∂t=H|ψ⟩ — Unitary time evolution for a closed system. Units: Both sides energy×state Conditions: Hamiltonian self-adjoint with appropriate domain; measurement/open-system dynamics require added framework.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Position-space Hamiltonian (Quantum Mechanics).
cards.back: H=−(ħ²/2m)∇²+V(r,t) — Kinetic plus multiplicative potential model. Units: J Conditions: No relativistic, spin, magnetic vector-potential or many-body terms unless added.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Normalization and Born probability (Quantum Mechanics).
cards.back: ∫|ψ|²dτ=1; P(R)=∫_R|ψ|²dτ — Total probability one and regional outcome probability. Units: |ψ|² inverse volume Conditions: Normalizable state; scattering eigenstates use delta normalization/wave packets.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Expectation and variance (Quantum Mechanics).
cards.back: ⟨A⟩=⟨ψ|A|ψ⟩; (ΔA)²=⟨A²⟩−⟨A⟩² — Predicted ensemble mean and spread. Units: A and A² Conditions: State in operator domains and moments finite.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Canonical commutator (Quantum Mechanics).
cards.back: [x,p_x]=iħ; p_x=−iħ∂/∂x — Position and momentum are noncommuting conjugates. Units: Action Conditions: Domains/boundaries matter; formal differential expression alone is not enough.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Robertson uncertainty (Quantum Mechanics).
cards.back: ΔAΔB≥½|⟨[A,B]⟩| — State-dependent lower bound from noncommutativity. Units: Product of A,B units Conditions: State lies in required domains; stronger Schrödinger relation includes covariance anticommutator term.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Probability continuity (Quantum Mechanics).
cards.back: ∂ρ/∂t+∇·j=0; ρ=|ψ|²; j=(ħ/m)Im(ψ*∇ψ) — Conservation of total probability. Units: ρ per volume, j per area-time Conditions: Modify for vector potentials/spin/other Hamiltonians.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Infinite-well energies (Quantum Mechanics).
cards.back: E_n=n²π²ħ²/(2mL²), ψ_n=√(2/L)sin(nπx/L) — Boundary conditions quantize standing-wave states. Units: E J Conditions: Infinite walls, nonrelativistic particle, one dimension.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Harmonic oscillator spectrum (Quantum Mechanics).
cards.back: E_n=(n+½)ħω; [a,a†]=1 — Equally spaced energy levels with nonzero ground energy. Units: J Conditions: Quadratic potential and standard nonrelativistic oscillator.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Angular momentum algebra (Quantum Mechanics).
cards.back: [L_i,L_j]=iħε_ijkL_k; L²|lm⟩=ħ²l(l+1)|lm⟩; L_z|lm⟩=ħm|lm⟩ — Rotational symmetry and quantized components. Units: Angular momentum Conditions: Orbital angular momentum representation; spin uses same algebra with half-integer possibilities.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Spin-½ operators (Quantum Mechanics).
cards.back: S=(ħ/2)σ; S_z outcomes ±ħ/2 — Two-dimensional intrinsic angular-momentum representation. Units: J·s Conditions: Measurement probabilities depend on state and chosen axis.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify First-order energy perturbation (Quantum Mechanics).
cards.back: E_n^(1)=⟨n⁰|H′|n⁰⟩ — Leading energy shift is diagonal perturbation expectation. Units: J Conditions: Nondegenerate case, perturbation small; degeneracy requires diagonalizing H′ in subspace.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify WKB forbidden-region factor (Quantum Mechanics).
cards.back: T∼exp[−2∫_{x₁}^{x₂}κ(x)dx], κ=√[2m(V−E)]/ħ — Semiclassical exponential suppression through smooth/wide barrier. Units: Exponent dimensionless Conditions: Slowly varying potential away from turning points and barrier exponent sufficiently large; prefactor omitted.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify de Broglie relation (Quantum Mechanics).
cards.back: p=ħk=h/λ — Momentum sets wave number/wavelength. Units: kg·m/s Conditions: For relativistic particles use relativistic p; wavelength does not mean particle is spatially sinusoidal everywhere.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Boltzmann entropy (Statistical Mechanics).
cards.back: S=k_B ln Ω — Entropy grows logarithmically with number of compatible microstates. Units: J/K Conditions: Microcanonical/equiprobable coarse-grained setting; additive constants/coarse graining stated.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Gibbs entropy (Statistical Mechanics).
cards.back: S=−k_BΣ_i p_i ln p_i — Entropy of a discrete probability distribution. Units: J/K Conditions: Classical/discrete ensemble; quantum version uses −k_BTrρlnρ.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Canonical probability (Statistical Mechanics).
cards.back: p_i=e^(−βE_i)/Z; β=1/(k_BT); Z=Σ_i e^(−βE_i) — Equilibrium occupation in energy bath. Units: Z dimensionless for discrete quantum states Conditions: Weak coupling to large bath, equilibrium, fixed V,N.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Canonical thermodynamics (Statistical Mechanics).
cards.back: U=−∂lnZ/∂β; F=−k_BT lnZ; S=k_B(lnZ+βU) — Partition function generates thermodynamic functions. Units: U,F J; S J/K Conditions: Energy zero changes Z/F consistently but not probabilities/derived differences.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Energy fluctuation (Statistical Mechanics).
cards.back: Var(E)=∂²lnZ/∂β²=k_BT²C_V — Heat capacity measures equilibrium energy fluctuations. Units: J² Conditions: Stable equilibrium, differentiable Z; finite-size/critical effects considered.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Grand partition function (Statistical Mechanics).
cards.back: Ξ=Σ_{N,i}e^{−β(E_{iN}−μN)}; Ω_G=−k_BT lnΞ=−PV — Generates particle number and pressure in homogeneous system. Units: Energy Conditions: Equilibrium grand canonical ensemble; Ω_G=−PV in thermodynamic homogeneous bulk.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Mean particle number (Statistical Mechanics).
cards.back: ⟨N⟩=(1/β)∂lnΞ/∂μ — Chemical-potential derivative gives occupation. Units: Count Conditions: Grand canonical equilibrium.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Maxwell–Boltzmann occupation (Statistical Mechanics).
cards.back: f_MB(E)≈e^{−β(E−μ)} — Classical limit of quantum distributions. Units: Mean occupation dimensionless Conditions: Mean occupation ≪1 or fugacity low; indistinguishability handled in partition function.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Bose/Fermi occupations (Statistical Mechanics).
cards.back: f_BE=1/[e^{β(E−μ)}−1]; f_FD=1/[e^{β(E−μ)}+1] — Bosons can share states; fermion occupation ≤1 per single-particle state. Units: Dimensionless Conditions: Ideal noninteracting gas; degeneracy and μ constraints stated.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Thermal de Broglie wavelength (Statistical Mechanics).
cards.back: λ_th=h/√(2πmk_BT) — Quantum wavepacket scale for thermal translational motion. Units: m Conditions: Nonrelativistic particles; classical dilute regime nλ_th³≪1.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify 3D free-particle density of states (Statistical Mechanics).
cards.back: g(E)=g_s V/(4π²)(2m/ħ²)^(3/2)√E — Available free-particle states grow as √E. Units: states per J Conditions: Large 3D box, continuum, nonrelativistic parabolic dispersion.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Free-electron Fermi energy (Statistical Mechanics).
cards.back: E_F=ħ²(3π²n)^(2/3)/(2m_e) — Highest occupied energy at T=0 ideal electron gas. Units: J or eV Conditions: 3D noninteracting electrons, parabolic dispersion.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Ideal-gas translational partition (Statistical Mechanics).
cards.back: Z_N=(V/λ_th³)^N/N! — Counts translational states with Gibbs factor. Units: Dimensionless Conditions: Dilute ideal gas, large N; internal states omitted.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Equipartition result (Statistical Mechanics).
cards.back: U=(f/2)Nk_BT; C_V=(f/2)Nk_B — Classical energy per quadratic term ½k_BT. Units: J and J/K Conditions: Classical canonical quadratic Hamiltonian; frozen quantum modes violate it.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Nuclear radius (Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection).
cards.back: R≈r₀A^(1/3), r₀≈1.2 fm — Approximately constant nuclear density scaling. Units: m or fm Conditions: Empirical bulk radius; halo/deformed/light nuclei can deviate.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Binding energy (Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection).
cards.back: B=[Zm_p+Nm_n−m_nucleus]c² — Mass defect measures nuclear binding. Units: J or MeV Conditions: Consistent mass convention and electron binding corrections where precision matters.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Semi-empirical mass formula (Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection).
cards.back: B≈a_vA−a_sA^(2/3)−a_cZ(Z−1)A^(−1/3)−a_a(A−2Z)²/A+δ — Liquid-drop trends in binding/stability. Units: MeV Conditions: Empirical smooth model; shell effects and light nuclei require corrections.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Radioactive decay (Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection).
cards.back: dN/dt=−λN; N=N₀e^(−λt); A=λN — Constant independent hazard gives exponential survival. Units: λ s⁻¹, A Bq Conditions: Single decay mode/constant environment unless branching or time dependence included.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Half-life/mean life (Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection).
cards.back: T₁/₂=ln2/λ; τ=1/λ — Characteristic survival times. Units: s Conditions: Do not confuse half-life with activity or time until all nuclei decay.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Parent-daughter chain (Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection).
cards.back: N₂(t)=λ₁N₁₀[e^(−λ₁t)−e^(−λ₂t)]/(λ₂−λ₁) for N₂(0)=0 — Daughter grows from parent and decays itself. Units: Count Conditions: No branching/feed, constant λ, distinct λ₁≠λ₂.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Reaction Q value (Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection).
cards.back: Q=(Σm_initial−Σm_final)c² — Rest-mass change appears in kinetic/excitation energy. Units: MeV Conditions: Conserve momentum; lab threshold can exceed −Q because recoil momentum is required.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Reaction rate (Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection).
cards.back: R=ΦN_tσ — Thin-target interaction expectation. Units: s⁻¹ Conditions: Uniform monoenergetic flux, negligible attenuation/multiple interactions; integrate over energy/geometry generally.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Exponential attenuation (Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection).
cards.back: I(x)=I₀e^(−μx); x_1/2=ln2/μ — Uncollided narrow-beam intensity under constant interaction probability per path. Units: μ inverse length Conditions: Monoenergetic narrow-beam idealization; buildup/scatter, spectrum and geometry alter detector reading.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Inverse-square fluence idealization (Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection).
cards.back: rate∝1/r² — Geometric spreading over sphere. Units: Ratio dimensionless Conditions: Point isotropic source, free space, same orientation, no attenuation/scatter; never replace facility survey/procedure.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Absorbed dose (Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection).
cards.back: D=dε̄/dm — Physical energy deposition per mass. Units: Gy=J/kg Conditions: Specify material/region and averaging; equivalent/effective dose are different protection quantities.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Equivalent dose (Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection).
cards.back: H_T=Σ_R w_R D_{T,R} — Radiation-quality-weighted absorbed dose to tissue/organ. Units: Sv Conditions: Protection quantity using prescribed factors, not direct biological measurement.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Multiplication factor (Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection).
cards.back: k_eff=neutrons in generation n+1 / neutrons in generation n — Subcritical <1, critical =1, supercritical >1. Units: Dimensionless Conditions: Reactor kinetics requires delayed neutrons, leakage, spectrum, geometry and feedback; no operational guidance implied.

cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Counting statistics ideal (Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection).
cards.back: u_N≈√N; u_R≈√N/t for N Poisson counts in time t — Independent count variance equals expected count. Units: Counts and s⁻¹ Conditions: Correct for background, dead time, efficiency, nonstationarity and low-count interval method.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Two-body equation (Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing).
cards.back: r̈=−μr/r³; μ=G(M+m)≈GM — Inverse-square central gravitational motion. Units: m/s² Conditions: Point/spherical bodies, isolated two-body; perturbations omitted.
