cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Specific energy and vis-viva (Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing).
cards.back: ε=v²/2−μ/r=−μ/(2a); v²=μ(2/r−1/a) — Relates speed, position and orbit size. Units: J/kg=m²/s² Conditions: Kepler two-body conic; for parabola a→∞ and ε=0.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Specific angular momentum (Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing).
cards.back: h=|r×v|; p=h²/μ=a(1−e²) — Sets plane and conic geometry. Units: m²/s Conditions: Central two-body force.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Kepler period (Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing).
cards.back: T=2π√(a³/μ) — Period depends on semimajor axis, not eccentricity, in two-body model. Units: s Conditions: Bound Kepler orbit around fixed μ.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Escape speed (Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing).
cards.back: v_esc=√(2μ/r) — Speed for zero specific energy. Units: m/s Conditions: No atmosphere/rotation/other bodies/propulsion after launch; local escape from central body idealization.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Hohmann transfer impulses (Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing).
cards.back: Δv₁=√(μ/r₁)[√(2r₂/(r₁+r₂))−1]; Δv₂=√(μ/r₂)[1−√(2r₁/(r₁+r₂))] — Two tangent burns enter/exit transfer ellipse. Units: m/s Conditions: Instantaneous impulses, circular coplanar orbits, two-body; signs reverse/absolute values for inward transfer.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Plane-change impulse (Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing).
cards.back: Δv=2v sin(Δi/2) — Vector difference between equal-speed velocity directions. Units: m/s Conditions: Best performed where speed low; combined burns can reduce cost.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Rocket equation (Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing).
cards.back: Δv=v_e ln(m₀/m_f)=I_sp g₀ ln(m₀/m_f) — Ideal momentum balance links mass ratio and velocity increment. Units: m/s Conditions: No external force/gravity/drag during derivation; system staging/finite burns and losses added separately.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Attitude angular momentum (Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing).
cards.back: H=Iω+h_w; τ_ext=dH/dt in inertial frame — External torque changes total body-plus-wheel angular momentum. Units: N·m·s Conditions: Rigid-body/tensor details and frame derivative handled; wheel saturation requires momentum unloading.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Radiative thermal balance (Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing).
cards.back: P_emit=εσAT⁴; P_abs=αSA_proj plus albedo/planet/internal terms — Spacecraft temperature follows absorbed, dissipated, conducted and emitted power. Units: W Conditions: Lumped steady approximation; view factors, transient nodes and wavelength dependence generally needed.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Free-space link relation (Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing).
cards.back: P_r=P_tG_tG_r(λ/4πR)²/L — Ideal link budget starting point. Units: W Conditions: Far-field line-of-sight, polarization/impedance/pointing handled, no unmodelled atmosphere/multipath.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Approximate ground sample distance (Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing).
cards.back: GSD≈H p/f — Projects pixel angular size to nadir ground scale. Units: m per pixel Conditions: Flat/nadir/small-angle approximation; pixel spacing is not full spatial resolution.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Radar range resolution (Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing).
cards.back: ΔR≈c/(2B) — Bandwidth controls ability to separate returns in slant range. Units: m Conditions: Pulse compression/waveform/processing/SNR/windowing affect practical resolution.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: State, interpret, and qualify Radiance calibration model (Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing).
cards.back: L_λ=(DN−offset)/gain with uncertainty and nonlinearity corrections — Converts instrument code to physical spectral radiance. Units: Radiance units Conditions: Actual calibration may be nonlinear/time/temperature dependent; product retrieval adds atmosphere/geometry/model.

cards.front: Correct this Solid State Physics claim: A diffraction peak proves the sample is pure.
cards.back: Discuss detection limits, overlap, amorphous content, texture, reference quality, and complementary evidence.

cards.front: Correct this Solid State Physics claim: Scherrer size is particle size.
cards.back: Call it an apparent coherent-domain size and state instrument/strain/shape assumptions.

cards.front: Correct this Solid State Physics claim: A band gap directly determines conductivity.
cards.back: Add Fermi level, carrier population, mobility, defects, contacts, and temperature.

cards.front: Correct this Solid State Physics claim: Hall coefficient always equals 1/(ne).
cards.back: State the single-carrier assumptions and consider multiband or anomalous response.

cards.front: Correct this Solid State Physics claim: A perfect lattice is enough to explain the sample.
cards.back: Include defects, surfaces, grain boundaries, finite size, strain, and thermal motion.

cards.front: Correct this Solid State Physics claim: Zero resistance alone proves superconductivity.
cards.back: Require magnetic response/Meissner evidence and rule out measurement floor or shorts.

cards.front: Correct this Solid State Physics claim: Peak intensity can be interpreted without geometry or texture.
cards.back: Mention structure factor, multiplicity, instrument corrections, absorption, and preferred orientation.

cards.front: Correct this Solid State Physics claim: Doping only changes carrier density.
cards.back: It can also change scattering, compensation, defects, band structure, and mobility.

cards.front: Correct this Materials Characterization claim: The image looks clear, so the instrument is calibrated.
cards.back: Image appearance is not traceable calibration; state scale reference, conditions, resolution, and uncertainty.

cards.front: Correct this Materials Characterization claim: No peak means the species is absent.
cards.back: State detection limit, overlap, selection rule, background, sampling, and confidence.

cards.front: Correct this Materials Characterization claim: One attractive micrograph represents the batch.
cards.back: Use predefined representative sampling across fields and independent batches with statistics.

cards.front: Correct this Materials Characterization claim: A Tauc straight line proves the band gap.
cards.back: State transition/absorption model, baseline/scattering/thickness, fit sensitivity, defects, and uncertainty.

cards.front: Correct this Materials Characterization claim: EDS gives exact stoichiometry automatically.
cards.back: Discuss standards/corrections, geometry, interaction volume, overlap, matrix, detection limits, and uncertainty.

cards.front: Correct this Materials Characterization claim: XPS is a bulk-composition technique.
cards.back: State surface sensitivity and surface history; use complementary bulk-sensitive evidence.

cards.front: Correct this Materials Characterization claim: A DSC peak uniquely identifies a phase transition.
cards.back: Check calibration, rate, atmosphere, cycling, TGA/decomposition, and before/after structural evidence.

cards.front: Correct this Materials Characterization claim: Software output is the measurement.
cards.back: Separate raw signal, preprocessing, model, fit, residuals, parameter uncertainty, and physical claim.

cards.front: Correct this Materials Characterization claim: Higher magnification means higher resolution.
cards.back: Magnification can enlarge unresolved information; resolution is set by probe, optics, interaction, detector, sample, and SNR.

cards.front: Correct this Materials Characterization claim: Complementary means repeating the same claim twice.
cards.back: Choose methods with different sensitivity or scale that test separate claims or competing explanations.

cards.front: Correct this Optics and Lasers claim: A laser is directional because stimulated emission is directional.
cards.back: Stimulated emission supplies coherent gain into modes; cavity geometry, aperture, and mode selection set beam direction/divergence.

cards.front: Correct this Optics and Lasers claim: Interference and diffraction are unrelated phenomena.
cards.back: Both are superposition; diffraction is often interference across a continuous finite aperture.

cards.front: Correct this Optics and Lasers claim: Higher magnification always means better resolution.
cards.back: Separate display scale from optical PSF, aperture, aberrations, sampling, and SNR.

cards.front: Correct this Optics and Lasers claim: Uncertainty in interference is just poor alignment.
cards.back: Coherence, bandwidth, source size, polarization, vibration, detector averaging, and noise all matter.

cards.front: Correct this Optics and Lasers claim: Total internal reflection means no field exists in the second medium.
cards.back: An evanescent field penetrates the lower-index medium even though no net propagating normal power exists in the ideal case.

cards.front: Correct this Optics and Lasers claim: At Brewster angle there is no reflected light.
cards.back: Only ideal p-polarized reflection vanishes; s polarization and nonideal media remain.

cards.front: Correct this Optics and Lasers claim: Rayleigh resolution is an absolute fundamental wall.
cards.back: Name the pupil/source/SNR/criterion; it is a conventional diffraction criterion.

cards.front: Correct this Optics and Lasers claim: Population inversion alone guarantees lasing.
cards.back: Net modal gain must exceed internal and output-coupling losses with feedback and mode overlap.

cards.front: Correct this Optics and Lasers claim: A narrow spectrum automatically proves coherence and single mode.
cards.back: Instrument resolution, line shape, phase noise, longitudinal/transverse modes, and measurement method matter.

cards.front: Correct this Optics and Lasers claim: Quantum efficiency and responsivity are the same.
cards.back: QE is carriers per photon; responsivity is electrical output per optical power and depends on photon energy and gain.

cards.front: Correct this Thermodynamics claim: Heat is energy stored in a hot object.
cards.back: Heat is transfer due to temperature difference; internal energy is a state property.

cards.front: Correct this Thermodynamics claim: Adiabatic means constant temperature.
cards.back: Adiabatic means no heat transfer; temperature can change through work.

cards.front: Correct this Thermodynamics claim: Adiabatic always means isentropic.
cards.back: Only reversible adiabatic is isentropic; irreversible adiabatic generates entropy.

cards.front: Correct this Thermodynamics claim: Quasistatic automatically means reversible.
cards.back: Check friction, finite gradients, viscosity, hysteresis and entropy generation.

cards.front: Correct this Thermodynamics claim: Entropy is just disorder.
cards.back: Use dS=δQ_rev/T, entropy balance, or a stated statistical multiplicity model.

cards.front: Correct this Thermodynamics claim: ΔG<0 means the reaction is fast.
cards.back: Separate thermodynamic direction under fixed T,P from kinetic barriers and transport.

cards.front: Correct this Thermodynamics claim: Carnot efficiency uses Celsius temperatures.
cards.back: Use absolute thermodynamic temperatures.

cards.front: Correct this Thermodynamics claim: COP above one violates energy conservation.
cards.back: COP measures heat moved per work, and the device also exchanges heat with the other reservoir.

cards.front: Correct this Thermodynamics claim: Q_p always equals ΔH.
cards.back: State closed system, constant pressure, only PV work and compatible kinetic/potential assumptions.

cards.front: Correct this Thermodynamics claim: A DSC peak uniquely identifies a phase transition.
cards.back: Check calibration, rate, cycling, TGA/decomposition, kinetics and before/after structural evidence.

cards.front: Correct this Basic Electronics and Instrumentation claim: A capacitor passes AC and blocks DC in every situation.
cards.back: Use i=C dv/dt or Z_C; transients, frequency, source/load, leakage and parasitics determine behavior.

cards.front: Correct this Basic Electronics and Instrumentation claim: The op-amp inputs are always equal.
cards.back: They are approximately equal only under stable negative feedback in linear operation with high loop gain.

cards.front: Correct this Basic Electronics and Instrumentation claim: Virtual ground is a real ground.
cards.back: It is a feedback-controlled potential and cannot be treated as a zero-impedance current return.

cards.front: Correct this Basic Electronics and Instrumentation claim: Negative feedback always improves stability.
cards.back: Check loop gain, phase margin, extra poles, delays and load.

cards.front: Correct this Basic Electronics and Instrumentation claim: Nominal ADC bits equal measurement accuracy.
cards.back: Include reference, noise, ENOB, offset/gain, INL/DNL, driver, timing and calibration.

cards.front: Correct this Basic Electronics and Instrumentation claim: Sampling above twice the displayed signal frequency prevents aliasing.
cards.back: Band-limit the entire analog input including noise/interference and allow filter transition margin.

cards.front: Correct this Basic Electronics and Instrumentation claim: A clean oscilloscope trace proves the circuit is clean.
cards.back: Scope/probe bandwidth, aliasing, averaging, coupling, clipping and loading can hide or create features.

cards.front: Correct this Basic Electronics and Instrumentation claim: Ground is zero volts everywhere.
cards.back: Real return paths have impedance; current creates voltage differences and loops.

cards.front: Correct this Basic Electronics and Instrumentation claim: Sensitivity means a sensor is good.
cards.back: Also require selectivity, noise, drift, hysteresis, linearity, range, response, calibration and reliability.

cards.front: Correct this Basic Electronics and Instrumentation claim: Averaging removes all noise and error.
cards.back: Independent random noise may average down; drift, correlation, 1/f noise and bias remain.

cards.front: Correct this Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty claim: Dimensions prove an equation is correct.
cards.back: Dimensional consistency is necessary only; constants, signs, vectors and functional form may still be wrong.

cards.front: Correct this Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty claim: Zero curl always guarantees a global potential.
cards.back: Check topology, singularities and domain connectivity.

cards.front: Correct this Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty claim: Every matrix has a full eigenvector basis.
cards.back: Defective/non-normal matrices may not be diagonalizable; use Jordan/Schur/SVD as appropriate.

cards.front: Correct this Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty claim: A high R² proves the model.
cards.back: Inspect residuals, uncertainty, domain, alternatives, causality and predictions.

cards.front: Correct this Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty claim: Standard deviation is total measurement uncertainty.
cards.back: Add calibration, systematic/model, resolution, environmental and covariance contributions.

cards.front: Correct this Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty claim: Repeating removes systematic error.
cards.back: Repetition improves random precision; bias needs calibration, design or independent method.

cards.front: Correct this Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty claim: Error bars always mean one standard deviation.
cards.back: State whether SD, SE, confidence, credible, coverage or other interval and how computed.

cards.front: Correct this Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty claim: Uncorrelated means independent.
cards.back: Independence implies zero covariance when moments exist, but zero covariance alone is weaker except special models.

cards.front: Correct this Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty claim: More decimal places improve accuracy.
cards.back: Round according to uncertainty and retain guard digits only during calculation.

cards.front: Correct this Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty claim: Code output is correct if it converges.
cards.back: Convergence checks numerics, not equations, units, boundary conditions, implementation or physical model.

cards.front: Correct this Classical Mechanics and Oscillations claim: Every force has an equal and opposite force on the same body.
cards.back: Newton’s third-law partner acts on the other interacting body; free-body diagrams include only forces on chosen system.

cards.front: Correct this Classical Mechanics and Oscillations claim: If velocity is zero, acceleration is zero.
cards.back: At a turning point velocity may vanish while force/acceleration is nonzero.

cards.front: Correct this Classical Mechanics and Oscillations claim: Momentum conservation means kinetic-energy conservation.
cards.back: Momentum and energy have different conditions; internal energy can increase.

cards.front: Correct this Classical Mechanics and Oscillations claim: Angular momentum is conserved because an object rotates.
cards.back: Require zero net external torque about specified origin.

cards.front: Correct this Classical Mechanics and Oscillations claim: Centrifugal force is a fundamental interaction.
cards.back: It is an inertial term in rotating coordinates; derive sign from acceleration transform.

cards.front: Correct this Classical Mechanics and Oscillations claim: Lagrangian is always T−V.
cards.back: T−V is common for natural conservative systems; velocity-dependent potentials, fields and constraints can modify form.

cards.front: Correct this Classical Mechanics and Oscillations claim: Hamiltonian always equals total energy.
cards.back: State regular transform and time-independent natural-coordinate conditions.

cards.front: Correct this Classical Mechanics and Oscillations claim: Resonance always occurs exactly at ω₀.
cards.back: Peak depends on damping, observable and model; displacement peak shifts with damping.

cards.front: Correct this Classical Mechanics and Oscillations claim: High Q is always good.
cards.back: High Q increases selectivity/sensitivity but slows settling and raises resonant vulnerability.

cards.front: Correct this Classical Mechanics and Oscillations claim: Group velocity always equals signal or energy velocity.
cards.back: Only under suitable narrowband/weak-loss conditions; anomalous/absorbing media require care.

cards.front: Correct this Electromagnetic Theory claim: Potential is the electric field.
cards.back: Potential is scalar energy per charge; E=−∇V in electrostatics.

cards.front: Correct this Electromagnetic Theory claim: D is always εE and H is always B/μ.
cards.back: Those are constitutive models; define free/bound split, linearity, anisotropy, dispersion and hysteresis.

cards.front: Correct this Electromagnetic Theory claim: Displacement current is charge crossing vacuum gap.
cards.back: It is time derivative of electric displacement/flux term; no conduction charge need cross gap.

cards.front: Correct this Electromagnetic Theory claim: A magnetic field always does no work in any system.
cards.back: Point-charge qv×B has zero instantaneous power, but induced E, moving media/circuits and field energy exchange can do work.

cards.front: Correct this Electromagnetic Theory claim: Normal E and tangential B are always continuous.
cards.back: Use D/E and H/B boundary conditions with free surface sources and material laws.

cards.front: Correct this Electromagnetic Theory claim: All EM waves are transverse everywhere.
cards.back: Vacuum plane waves are transverse; near fields, guided modes, plasmas and anisotropic media can have longitudinal components.

cards.front: Correct this Electromagnetic Theory claim: Free-space path loss means vacuum absorbs power.
cards.back: It mainly represents geometric spreading/effective aperture in ideal vacuum link relation.

cards.front: Correct this Electromagnetic Theory claim: Poynting vector is energy density.
cards.back: S is energy flux W/m²; u is energy density J/m³.

cards.front: Correct this Electromagnetic Theory claim: Skin depth is exact for every conductor.
cards.back: The simple square-root formula needs good-conductor, homogeneous linear assumptions and ignores geometry/proximity.

cards.front: Correct this Electromagnetic Theory claim: High antenna gain creates power.
cards.back: Gain redistributes radiated power and includes efficiency; narrower beam trades angular coverage.

cards.front: Correct this Quantum Mechanics claim: Wavefunction is a classical physical wave.
cards.back: It is a complex state amplitude; Born rule and measurement define observable predictions.

cards.front: Correct this Quantum Mechanics claim: Measurement probability is ψ.
cards.back: Probability density is |ψ|² in position basis; amplitudes can be complex/negative.

cards.front: Correct this Quantum Mechanics claim: Uncertainty is poor instrument accuracy.
cards.back: Quantum state has intrinsic spread; apparatus adds separate uncertainty/disturbance.

cards.front: Correct this Quantum Mechanics claim: Energy eigenstate wavefunction is time independent.
cards.back: It acquires phase e^(−iEt/ħ); probability density is stationary.

cards.front: Correct this Quantum Mechanics claim: Tunnelling borrows energy.
cards.back: Total energy remains conserved in time-independent elastic tunnelling; forbidden-region amplitude is evanescent.

cards.front: Correct this Quantum Mechanics claim: Hermitian differential expression automatically defines observable.
cards.back: Domain and self-adjoint boundary conditions are essential.

cards.front: Correct this Quantum Mechanics claim: Every observable has a definite value before measurement in the formal state.
cards.back: State generally gives probability distribution; interpretation claims must be separated from operational predictions.

cards.front: Correct this Quantum Mechanics claim: Spin is a tiny ball rotating.
cards.back: Spin is intrinsic angular momentum representation with no consistent classical rigid-body model.

cards.front: Correct this Quantum Mechanics claim: Pauli principle is a repulsive force.
cards.back: It follows antisymmetry of identical fermion state, not a separate force.

cards.front: Correct this Quantum Mechanics claim: Variational result proves trial wavefunction is accurate.
cards.back: It bounds ground energy; wavefunction/other observables may still be poor.

cards.front: Correct this Statistical Mechanics claim: Partition function is only normalization.
cards.back: Its logarithm and derivatives generate energy, free energy, entropy, pressure, number and fluctuations.

cards.front: Correct this Statistical Mechanics claim: All microstates are equally probable in every ensemble.
cards.back: Equal a priori applies microcanonical; canonical weights depend on energy.

cards.front: Correct this Statistical Mechanics claim: Equipartition always gives ½kT per degree.
cards.back: Only active classical quadratic Hamiltonian terms; quantum gaps freeze modes.

cards.front: Correct this Statistical Mechanics claim: Fermi energy is average electron energy.
cards.back: It is highest occupied T=0 energy; average is 3E_F/5 in ideal 3D gas.

cards.front: Correct this Statistical Mechanics claim: Fluctuations disappear for macroscopic systems.
cards.back: Relative fluctuations often shrink; absolute fluctuations remain and critical scaling can differ.

cards.front: Correct this Statistical Mechanics claim: MB, BE and FD are different forces.
cards.back: They are occupation statistics from distinguishability/symmetry and dilute limit.

cards.front: Correct this Statistical Mechanics claim: Chemical potential is always positive.
cards.back: Sign depends energy reference/system; classical ideal gas μ often negative, photons equilibrium μ=0.

cards.front: Correct this Statistical Mechanics claim: Entropy means disorder only.
cards.back: Use multiplicity/probability/thermodynamic definition under stated constraints.

cards.front: Correct this Statistical Mechanics claim: Ensemble average automatically equals time average.
cards.back: Requires ergodic/mixing assumptions and sufficient observation relative correlation times.

cards.front: Correct this Statistical Mechanics claim: A straight Boltzmann plot proves equilibrium.
cards.back: Correct degeneracy, selection, opacity, calibration, range and nonequilibrium alternatives.

cards.front: Correct this Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection claim: Half-life is time until all nuclei decay.
cards.back: It is time for expected population/activity to halve; exponential never reaches exact zero.

cards.front: Correct this Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection claim: Activity and dose are interchangeable.
cards.back: Activity Bq is decay rate; dose Gy/Sv depends energy deposition, radiation/tissue and geometry.

cards.front: Correct this Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection claim: Cross section is geometric nucleus area or probability.
cards.back: It is rate measure with area units; probability also needs target density/path/flux.

cards.front: Correct this Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection claim: Critical reactor means accident.
cards.back: Critical means k_eff=1 average steady generations; operating safety needs full engineered context.

cards.front: Correct this Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection claim: XRD or one detector peak proves isotope/phase purity.
cards.back: State detection limits, response, mixtures, branching, overlap and complementary evidence.

cards.front: Correct this Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection claim: Shielding is just use densest material.
cards.back: Particle/energy interactions, secondary radiation, geometry and qualified design determine approach.

cards.front: Correct this Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection claim: I can demonstrate radiation concepts with any available source.
cards.back: Never handle or improvise; only authorized sources, facilities, procedures and supervision.

cards.front: Correct this Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection claim: Contamination and irradiation are same.
cards.back: Contamination is radioactive material present; irradiation is field exposure.

cards.front: Correct this Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection claim: Poisson √N is always total uncertainty.
cards.back: Include background, dead time, efficiency, drift, geometry and interval method.

cards.front: Correct this Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection claim: ALARA means zero exposure at any cost.
cards.back: It is optimization within justified regulated practice, not a standalone numerical rule.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: Correct this Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing claim: Orbit altitude determines period alone.
cards.back: Use semimajor axis and central μ; distinguish altitude from radius and circular from elliptical.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: Correct this Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing claim: A satellite remains in orbit because there is no gravity.
cards.back: It is continuously falling under gravity with tangential velocity.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: Correct this Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing claim: Geostationary means any 24-hour orbit.
cards.back: Require circular, equatorial, prograde and sidereal period.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: Correct this Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing claim: Hohmann is always best.
cards.back: It is ideal two-impulse result for coplanar circular orbits, not always time/Δv/operations optimum.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: Correct this Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing claim: Reaction wheel provides unlimited control.
cards.back: Momentum storage saturates; unloading/external torque and power limits matter.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: Correct this Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing claim: Vacuum means spacecraft cannot overheat.
cards.back: Radiation is only external heat rejection and internal/solar loads can raise temperature.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: Correct this Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing claim: More pixels means better resolution.
cards.back: Include optics MTF/diffraction, SNR, motion, atmosphere and sampling.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: Correct this Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing claim: Remote-sensing DN is physical radiance automatically.
cards.back: Apply calibration, dark/nonlinearity, atmosphere, geometry and uncertainty.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: Correct this Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing claim: SAR image is a photograph.
cards.back: It is coherent microwave backscatter product shaped by geometry, polarization, surface and processing.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: Correct this Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing claim: Redundancy guarantees reliability.
cards.back: Check common cause, switching, complexity, qualification, resources and recovery logic.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Bragg’s law from path difference.
cards.back: Adjacent-plane path difference is 2d sinθ; integer-wavelength phase matching produces a diffraction maximum. Assumptions: Parallel lattice planes separated by d; Elastic scattering with wavelength λ; Specular geometry for the selected planes; Far-field interference Common mistake: Using the instrument’s displayed 2θ in place of θ, or treating every peak as first order without indexing.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Drude conductivity in the relaxation-time model.
cards.back: Balance field acceleration against momentum relaxation, then convert drift velocity to current density. Assumptions: One carrier type; Uniform weak electric field; Parabolic band represented by m*; Collisions randomize momentum with mean time τ; Steady state Common mistake: Using the bare electron mass automatically or treating τ as the time between all microscopic interactions without model qualification.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Single-carrier Hall coefficient.
cards.back: Transverse electric force balances magnetic deflection; current density links drift speed to carrier density. Assumptions: Rectangular sample with current x, field z, Hall voltage y; One carrier type with signed charge q; Steady transverse force balance; Uniform current density and field Common mistake: Computing mobility from Hall coefficient alone; μ requires conductivity/resistivity too.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Beer–Lambert exponential attenuation.
cards.back: A constant fractional loss per distance integrates to exponential attenuation. Assumptions: Homogeneous medium; Independent constant loss probability per unit length; No source term; Fixed wavelength and geometry Common mistake: Calling all lost transmission absorption or applying a Tauc transform without correcting scattering/baseline and defining α.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Bragg condition for XRD.
cards.back: Adjacent-plane path difference equals 2d sinθ; integer phase matching gives a peak. Assumptions: Parallel planes; Elastic monochromatic scattering; Far-field phase comparison; Known angle convention Common mistake: Using 2θ as θ or calling a database match proof of purity.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Hall voltage and mobility from combined measurements.
cards.back: Balance transverse forces for R_H, then combine with longitudinal conductivity for mobility. Assumptions: One dominant carrier; Rectangular homogeneous specimen; Perpendicular current and magnetic field; Linear response; Known thickness Common mistake: Inferring mobility from Hall voltage without thickness, field, current, and conductivity or ignoring contact-offset removal.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Fraunhofer diffraction from a uniform single slit.
cards.back: Integrate phase across the slit; the amplitude is sinc and intensity is sinc squared. Assumptions: Scalar monochromatic wave; Uniform field across slit width a; Far field or focal plane of a lens; Paraxial phase relation where used Common mistake: Calling θ=0 a minimum or using screen coordinate y without stating tanθ≈y/L.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Brewster angle from Fresnel geometry.
cards.back: Set the p-polarized Fresnel reflection to zero, combine perpendicular-ray geometry with Snell’s law, and obtain tanθ_B=n₂/n₁. Assumptions: Planar boundary; Lossless isotropic nonmagnetic dielectrics; p polarization; Real positive refractive indices Common mistake: Saying all reflected light vanishes; only the ideal p component does.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Laser threshold from round-trip gain.
cards.back: Multiply gain and losses around one cavity trip; threshold occurs when the product is exactly one. Assumptions: Linear unsaturated intensity gain g; Uniform internal intensity loss α_i; Cavity length L; Mirror intensity reflectivities R₁,R₂; One-dimensional round trip Common mistake: Using amplitude reflectivity in an intensity formula or ignoring output coupling as a loss and useful output simultaneously.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Carnot efficiency from reservoir entropy balance.
cards.back: Use first-law cyclic energy balance and reversible reservoir entropy balance to eliminate Q_C/Q_H. Assumptions: Reversible cyclic engine; Two reservoirs at T_H and T_C; Heat Q_H absorbed and Q_C rejected as positive magnitudes; Working substance returns to initial state Common mistake: Using Celsius or claiming Carnot describes a practical engine’s detailed cycle.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Maxwell relations from thermodynamic potentials.
cards.back: Write each potential differential, identify conjugate derivatives, and equate mixed partials. Assumptions: Equilibrium simple compressible closed system; Potentials are state functions with continuous mixed second derivatives; Composition fixed for the displayed relations Common mistake: Memorizing signs without writing the differential and natural variables.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Clapeyron equation at phase coexistence.
cards.back: Differentiate equality of molar Gibbs energies along coexistence and substitute dg=−s dT+v dP. Assumptions: Two phases α and β in equilibrium; Single component; Coexistence line P(T); Molar Gibbs energies equal Common mistake: Using the ideal-vapor Clausius approximation for solid–solid or liquid–solid transitions.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for RC charging from Kirchhoff’s law.
cards.back: KVL plus i=C dv/dt gives a first-order equation with exponential approach to final voltage. Assumptions: Ideal DC step V_s; Series R and C; Capacitor initial voltage V_0; No parasitic/loading changes Common mistake: Assuming τ uses any visible resistor rather than the Thevenin resistance seen by the capacitor.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Ideal inverting op-amp gain.
cards.back: Use virtual short plus zero input current, apply KCL at the summing node, and obtain the resistor-ratio gain. Assumptions: Infinite open-loop gain in stable negative feedback; Input currents zero; V_+=0 and virtual short V_−≈V_+; Output not saturated and bandwidth adequate Common mistake: Calling the inverting node a real ground capable of supplying current, or ignoring common-mode/output range.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Closed-loop gain and desensitivity.
cards.back: Write error subtraction and forward gain, solve algebraically, then take the large-loop-gain limit. Assumptions: Linear scalar forward gain A; Feedback signal βV_o subtracted from source; Stable operation; Frequency dependence suppressed until final discussion Common mistake: Saying negative feedback always improves stability without checking frequency-dependent loop phase and margins.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for First-order uncertainty propagation with covariance.
cards.back: Linearize the output around input means, then propagate the covariance matrix through the gradient. Assumptions: Inputs fluctuate near means; f differentiable; Taylor expansion adequate; Covariance matrix represents input uncertainties Common mistake: Adding percentage uncertainties linearly or ignoring shared calibration correlations.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Ordinary least-squares slope and intercept.
cards.back: Minimize squared vertical residuals, solve the two normal equations, and express them using centered data. Assumptions: Model y_i=a+bx_i+ε_i; x values treated exact; Equal weighting; Minimize vertical residual squares Common mistake: Using ordinary least squares when x uncertainty is important or interpreting R² as causation.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Fourier derivative property.
cards.back: Integrate the derivative transform by parts; differentiation becomes multiplication by ik. Assumptions: Transform convention F(k)=∫f(x)e^(−ikx)dx; f and derivative sufficiently well behaved; Boundary term vanishes or distributions handled correctly Common mistake: Forgetting transform convention sign/2π factors or boundary terms.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Work-energy theorem.
cards.back: Dot Newton’s law with velocity and integrate; power from net force is time derivative of kinetic energy. Assumptions: Particle of constant mass; Inertial frame; Differentiable trajectory; Net force includes all modeled forces Common mistake: Using one force’s work as total work or ignoring frame-dependent kinetic energy/work.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Euler–Lagrange equation from stationary action.
cards.back: Vary the action, integrate velocity variation by parts, use fixed endpoints, and invoke arbitrary coordinate variation. Assumptions: Action S=∫L(q,q̇,t)dt; Allowed variation q→q+εη with η endpoints zero; L differentiable; Constraints already incorporated or treated separately Common mistake: Saying nature chooses the path with minimum L at every instant or forgetting fixed endpoint variation.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Effective potential for central-force motion.
cards.back: Use angular-momentum conservation to eliminate angular speed and rewrite energy as radial kinetic plus effective potential. Assumptions: Potential V(r) depends only on radius; Planar polar coordinates; Time-independent system; Particle/reduced mass m Common mistake: Treating centrifugal barrier as a new physical central force without stating reduced radial description.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Electromagnetic wave equation from Maxwell equations.
cards.back: Curl Faraday, substitute Ampère–Maxwell, use vector identity and source-free divergence. Assumptions: Source-free vacuum ρ=0,J=0; Homogeneous ε₀,μ₀; Fields sufficiently smooth Common mistake: Setting divergence E to zero without stating source-free region or claiming all EM waves are plane waves.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Poynting theorem.
cards.back: Combine dotted curl equations with the divergence identity to obtain local field-energy conservation. Assumptions: Microscopic/vacuum Maxwell form; Fields and currents smooth enough; Fixed spatial coordinates Common mistake: Treating S as energy density rather than flux, or ignoring sign of J·E.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Electromagnetic boundary conditions.
cards.back: Use pillboxes for normal components and shrinking loops for tangential components, retaining allowed surface charge/current. Assumptions: Interface with unit normal from medium 1 to 2; Fields finite near interface except allowed surface sources; Infinitesimal pillbox/loop limits Common mistake: Saying normal E or tangential B is always continuous regardless of material/surface sources.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Infinite square-well eigenstates and energies.
cards.back: Solve sinusoidal interior equation, impose two zero boundaries, normalize, and read discrete k and E. Assumptions: One-dimensional 0<x<L; V=0 inside and infinite outside; ψ(0)=ψ(L)=0; Nonrelativistic spinless particle Common mistake: Allowing n=0 or saying particle literally follows standing-wave trajectory.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Robertson uncertainty relation.
cards.back: Apply Cauchy–Schwarz to centered operator states and isolate commutator contribution. Assumptions: Normalized state; A and B self-adjoint on appropriate domains; Finite variances Common mistake: Writing ΔxΔp=ħ/2 as equality for every state.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Exponential tunnelling factor through a rectangular barrier.
cards.back: Forbidden-region wave decays with κ; crossing width a suppresses amplitude e^{−κa} and probability approximately e^{−2κa}. Assumptions: One-dimensional barrier width a; E<V₀; Nonrelativistic stationary state; Thick-barrier/WKB leading exponential; prefactor not derived Common mistake: Calling e^{−2κa} exact for every barrier or claiming particle borrows energy.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Canonical distribution from a large reservoir.
cards.back: Count bath states, expand bath entropy, identify β, and normalize with Z. Assumptions: Small subsystem weakly coupled to much larger isolated bath; Total energy fixed; Bath entropy smooth; Equal total microstate probability Common mistake: Assuming subsystem energies are equally probable in canonical ensemble.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Energy and free energy from partition function.
cards.back: Differentiate lnZ for U, insert Boltzmann probabilities into entropy, and recover F=−kTlnZ. Assumptions: Canonical Z=Σe^{−βE_i}; Energy levels β-independent; Differentiation/sum interchange valid Common mistake: Differentiating with respect to T without tracking β and fixed variables.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Fermi energy of a 3D free-electron gas.
cards.back: Count occupied k states inside a spin-degenerate sphere and convert k_F to energy. Assumptions: T=0; Noninteracting electrons; 3D volume V with periodic/box continuum; Spin degeneracy 2; Parabolic dispersion E=ħ²k²/2m Common mistake: Calling E_F the average energy; at T=0 average is 3E_F/5 for ideal 3D gas.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Exponential radioactive decay law.
cards.back: Constant fractional loss gives a first-order differential equation and exponential population/activity. Assumptions: Each nucleus has constant decay probability per unit time λ; Nuclei act independently; No production/feed or changing environment Common mistake: Saying activity stays constant or all nuclei decay after one half-life.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Two-member Bateman parent–daughter solution.
cards.back: Solve driven first-order daughter equation using parent exponential and integrating factor. Assumptions: Parent 1 decays only to daughter 2; Daughter decay constant λ₂; N₂(0)=0; No branching/removal Common mistake: Equating parent/daughter numbers when equilibrium refers approximately to activities.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Exponential narrow-beam attenuation.
cards.back: Constant fractional removal per distance integrates to exponential uncollided intensity. Assumptions: Monoenergetic narrow beam; Homogeneous material; Constant independent removal probability μ per path; Scattered particles excluded from detector Common mistake: Treating attenuation as absorbed dose or using one μ for mixed spectrum/geometry.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Vis-viva equation from orbital energy.
cards.back: Equate instantaneous specific energy to the conic’s constant −μ/2a and solve for speed. Assumptions: Two-body gravity; Specific energy conserved; Bound ellipse relation ε=−μ/(2a) Common mistake: Using altitude instead of geocentric radius or applying to powered/perturbed motion blindly.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Hohmann transfer impulses.
cards.back: Use one ellipse tangent to both circles, calculate its endpoint speeds with vis-viva, and difference from circular speeds. Assumptions: Initial/final circular coplanar orbits r₁,r₂; Tangent two-impulse ellipse; Instantaneous burns; Two-body gravity Common mistake: Calling it universally minimum Δv/time or forgetting circularization burn.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Tsiolkovsky rocket equation.
cards.back: Apply momentum conservation to infinitesimal expelled mass and integrate dm/m. Assumptions: Variable-mass vehicle in inertial frame; Effective exhaust speed constant relative vehicle; No external forces during differential derivation; One-dimensional collinear exhaust Common mistake: Treating rocket equation as thrust or including propellant mass with wrong initial/final definition.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Point-charge field from Gauss's law.
cards.back: Use spherical symmetry to make E constant on the Gaussian sphere, equate flux E4πr² to q/ε₀, and recover the inverse-square field. Assumptions: Static point charge q; Vacuum; Spherical symmetry; Gaussian sphere centred on charge Common mistake: Pulling E outside the flux integral for a surface where the magnitude is not constant.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Parallel-plate capacitance and stored energy.
cards.back: Find uniform field from surface charge, integrate to voltage, form Q/V, then integrate charging work. Assumptions: Two large parallel plates; Gap d much smaller than lateral dimensions; Uniform linear dielectric ε; Fringing neglected Common mistake: Using the uniform-field formula when fringing, nonlinear dielectric response, or electrode geometry dominates.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Magnetic field inside an ideal long solenoid.
cards.back: Use a rectangular Ampère loop and the ideal inside/outside field symmetry to obtain B=μ₀nI. Assumptions: Very long tightly wound solenoid; n turns per unit length; Steady current I; Vacuum or linear core stated; End effects neglected Common mistake: Claiming the external field is exactly zero for a finite solenoid.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Thin-film reflected interference condition.
cards.back: Compute the round-trip optical path, convert it to phase, add interface phase reversals, then impose total phase conditions. Assumptions: Plane-parallel film of thickness t and index n; Monochromatic coherent illumination; Internal angle θ_t; Reflection phase shifts tracked from index ordering Common mistake: Writing 2nt=mλ as the bright condition without checking reflection phase reversals.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Reversible adiabatic ideal-gas relation.
cards.back: Set heat to zero, express dU with C_V, substitute the ideal-gas equation, integrate, and use γ=C_P/C_V. Assumptions: Ideal gas; Reversible adiabatic path; Constant heat capacities; Only pressure-volume work Common mistake: Calling every adiabatic process isentropic or using Celsius temperature.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Small-oscillation frequency from a potential minimum.
cards.back: Taylor-expand the potential around a stable minimum; the quadratic curvature becomes the effective spring constant. Assumptions: One coordinate x; Stable equilibrium x₀; Potential twice differentiable; Displacement small enough for quadratic truncation; Constant mass m Common mistake: Using the approximation when V''=0 or displacement is large enough that cubic/quartic terms dominate.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Quantum harmonic-oscillator spectrum with ladder operators.
cards.back: Factor H into ladder operators, use their commutator, require a lowest normalizable state, and build equally spaced levels. Assumptions: One-dimensional Hamiltonian H=p²/(2m)+½mω²x²; Canonical commutator [x,p]=iħ; Normalized states and proper operator domains Common mistake: Assuming n can be negative or saying ground energy violates energy conservation.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Bohr-model hydrogen energy levels.
cards.back: Combine Coulomb force with angular-momentum quantization, find allowed radii, then evaluate total energy. Assumptions: Nonrelativistic electron in circular Coulomb orbit; Infinite nuclear mass approximation; Angular momentum quantization mvr=nħ; No spin, radiation, or relativistic corrections Common mistake: Presenting Bohr orbits as exact quantum trajectories or applying −13.6 eV/n² to multi-electron atoms unchanged.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Continuity equation from local conservation.
cards.back: Write integral conservation for an arbitrary fixed volume, convert boundary flux to volume divergence, and equate integrands. Assumptions: Conserved scalar density ρ; Flux J; Fixed control volume; Sufficient smoothness Common mistake: Using the source-free equation when production, loss, reactions, or moving control volumes are present.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Diffusion equation from Fick's law.
cards.back: Combine local conservation with Fick's gradient-driven flux and simplify for constant diffusivity. Assumptions: Conserved concentration c; Fickian flux J=−D∇c; Constant scalar diffusivity D; No sources or bulk flow Common mistake: Using constant-D diffusion in systems with reactions, drift, advection, or anomalous transport.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Heat equation from energy conservation and Fourier's law.
cards.back: Apply local energy conservation to Fourier heat flux and identify thermal diffusivity. Assumptions: Homogeneous stationary solid; Constant density ρ_m, heat capacity c_p, conductivity k; No internal heat source; Local thermal equilibrium Common mistake: Confusing thermal conductivity k with diffusivity α or ignoring boundary heat transfer.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Monostatic radar range equation scaling.
cards.back: Apply transmit spreading, target reradiation via σ, return spreading, and receive effective aperture to obtain R⁻⁴ power. Assumptions: Far-field free-space propagation; Monostatic radar; Target radar cross section σ; Matched polarization and stated losses omitted initially; Antenna gain G used on transmit and receive Common mistake: Treating radar cross section as physical area or using the equation without far-field, loss, noise, and detection assumptions.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Telescope light-gathering and diffraction scaling.
cards.back: Aperture area gives D² photon collection, while circular-pupil diffraction gives angular scale approximately 1.22λ/D. Assumptions: Circular clear aperture diameter D; Uniform illumination for Airy coefficient; Distant unresolved source; Same throughput when comparing ideal apertures Common mistake: Equating pixel count or magnification with optical resolution and ignoring central obstruction/seeing.

cards.front: Give the one-minute derivation outline for Inverse-variance weighted mean from Gaussian likelihood.
cards.back: Write the independent Gaussian likelihood, minimize chi-square, solve the normal equation, and read uncertainty from total weight. Assumptions: Independent measurements x_i of one common value μ; Known Gaussian standard uncertainties u_i; No extra heterogeneity or correlation; Unbiased measurements Common mistake: Using inverse-variance weights when measurements disagree beyond stated uncertainties or share calibration bias.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Solid State Physics: What is the difference between a lattice and a crystal structure?
cards.back: A lattice is a periodic point set; a crystal structure is lattice plus basis.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Materials Characterization: What is the first sentence of any instrument answer?
cards.back: Name the probe, physical interaction, and detected signal.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Optics and Lasers: When is ray optics valid?
cards.back: When wavelength is small relative to relevant structures and diffraction/interference can be neglected for the required accuracy.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Thermodynamics: State the zeroth law.
cards.back: If A and B are each in thermal equilibrium with C, they are in thermal equilibrium with each other; this supports empirical temperature.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Basic Electronics and Instrumentation: State Kirchhoff’s current law.
cards.back: Algebraic sum of currents at a lumped node is zero, following charge conservation when node charge accumulation is included in elements.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty: Why can dimensional analysis not find every constant?
cards.back: Dimensionless numerical factors/functions are unconstrained by dimensions alone.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Classical Mechanics and Oscillations: State Newton’s first law.
cards.back: In an inertial frame, a body with zero net force maintains constant velocity.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Electromagnetic Theory: Field versus potential?
cards.back: E is force per charge; electrostatic V is scalar energy per charge with E=−∇V.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Quantum Mechanics: What does a wavefunction represent?
cards.back: A state amplitude in chosen basis; Born rule gives probabilities from its modulus squared.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Statistical Mechanics: Microstate versus macrostate?
cards.back: Microstate is full microscopic specification; macrostate gives coarse thermodynamic variables.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection: Isotope versus isobar?
cards.back: Isotopes share Z; isobars share A.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing: What is two-body problem?
cards.back: Relative motion of two masses under mutual central gravity, reducible to one body with μ=G(M+m).

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Solid State Physics: Why are there fourteen three-dimensional Bravais lattices?
cards.back: They are the distinct translation lattices compatible with three-dimensional space-group symmetry, after equivalent choices are removed.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Materials Characterization: Accuracy versus precision?
cards.back: Accuracy concerns bias relative to a reference; precision concerns repeated spread.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Optics and Lasers: What is optical path length?
cards.back: OPL=∫n ds; it converts propagation through refractive media into phase accumulation.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Thermodynamics: Heat versus temperature?
cards.back: Heat is energy transfer due to temperature difference; temperature is a state variable related to equilibrium and energy distribution.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Basic Electronics and Instrumentation: State Kirchhoff’s voltage law.
cards.back: Algebraic sum of element voltage changes around a lumped loop is zero under the quasistatic circuit model.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty: Are radians dimensionless?
cards.back: Yes as a ratio of lengths, though rad is retained for clarity and angular-frequency mistakes remain possible.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Classical Mechanics and Oscillations: Why must a free-body diagram isolate one system?
cards.back: Forces are interactions on that chosen system; mixing action-reaction partners double-counts or misassigns forces.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Electromagnetic Theory: When is electric potential globally useful?
cards.back: Electrostatic/curl-free E in appropriate domain; time-varying E generally also needs vector potential.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Quantum Mechanics: Why normalize ψ?
cards.back: Total probability for a normalizable prepared state must be one.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Statistical Mechanics: What is multiplicity?
cards.back: Number/measure of accessible microstates compatible with constraints.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection: What is mass defect?
cards.back: Difference between separated constituent masses and bound-system mass, converted to binding energy.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing: State Kepler’s first law.
cards.back: Bound planetary two-body orbit is ellipse with central body at one focus.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Solid State Physics: What do Miller indices label?
cards.back: A family/orientation of lattice planes through reciprocals of axis intercepts, after clearing fractions.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Materials Characterization: Resolution versus sensitivity?
cards.back: Resolution separates nearby features; sensitivity is output change per measurand change.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Optics and Lasers: What does Snell’s law conserve?
cards.back: Tangential wavevector/phase matching across a planar interface.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Thermodynamics: State function versus path function?
cards.back: State-function change depends only on endpoints; heat and work depend on process path.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Basic Electronics and Instrumentation: What is a time constant?
cards.back: Characteristic exponential response time; for a first-order RC circuit τ=R_Thevenin C.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty: Gradient physical meaning?
cards.back: Direction and rate of steepest local increase of a scalar field.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Classical Mechanics and Oscillations: Mass versus weight?
cards.back: Mass measures inertia/system matter parameter; weight is gravitational force and depends on field/frame.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Electromagnetic Theory: What does divergence E mean?
cards.back: Local charge-source density through ∇·E=ρ/ε₀ in microscopic vacuum form.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Quantum Mechanics: Is ψ directly observable?
cards.back: Not as a classical field value; observable probabilities/expectations arise through measurement operators, though state tomography can infer it from ensembles.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Statistical Mechanics: Boltzmann entropy?
cards.back: S=k_B lnΩ for equiprobable microcanonical multiplicity.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection: Why binding energy per nucleon?
cards.back: Compares broad stability/energy-release trends across different A, not sole stability criterion.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing: Kepler’s second law meaning?
cards.back: Equal areas in equal times, equivalent to conserved specific angular momentum.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Solid State Physics: What is reciprocal space physically useful for?
cards.back: It represents periodicity and wavevector/momentum transfer, turning diffraction conditions into geometric relations.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Materials Characterization: What is calibration?
cards.back: A documented relation between indication and reference values with conditions and uncertainty.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Optics and Lasers: Two conditions for total internal reflection?
cards.back: Propagation from higher to lower refractive index and incidence above the critical angle.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Thermodynamics: What sign convention is used here?
cards.back: Heat into system positive, work done by system positive: dU=δQ−δW_by.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Basic Electronics and Instrumentation: Why does capacitor voltage not jump ideally?
cards.back: A finite jump would require an impulse/infinite current because i=C dv/dt.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty: Divergence physical meaning?
cards.back: Local net outward flux per volume in the limit.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Classical Mechanics and Oscillations: Static versus kinetic friction?
cards.back: Static friction adjusts up to a limit; kinetic friction is a sliding model, neither universally equals μN.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Electromagnetic Theory: What does curl E mean?
cards.back: Local circulation; Faraday law links it to changing B.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Quantum Mechanics: Global versus relative phase?
cards.back: Global phase does not change pure-state predictions; relative phase between components affects interference.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Statistical Mechanics: Why logarithm in entropy?
cards.back: Independent multiplicities multiply while extensive entropies add, so log converts products to sums.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection: What are magic numbers?
cards.back: Closed-shell nucleon counts associated with enhanced stability patterns.

cards.topic: Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing
cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Orbital Mechanics, Spacecraft Systems, and Remote Sensing: Kepler’s third law?
cards.back: T²=4π²a³/μ for a two-body bound orbit.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Solid State Physics: What is the first Brillouin zone?
cards.back: The Wigner–Seitz cell around the origin of the reciprocal lattice.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Materials Characterization: Why run a blank?
cards.back: To measure background, substrate, reagent, or instrument contribution without the target sample response.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Optics and Lasers: What is the Brewster angle?
cards.back: Ideal incidence angle at which reflected p-polarized amplitude vanishes; tanθ_B=n₂/n₁ for lossless nonmagnetic dielectrics.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Thermodynamics: What is internal energy?
cards.back: A state function containing microscopic kinetic, interaction and other internal contributions included in the system model, excluding bulk reference choices as stated.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Basic Electronics and Instrumentation: Why does inductor current not jump ideally?
cards.back: A finite jump would require an impulse/infinite voltage because v=L di/dt.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Mathematical Foundations, Data, and Uncertainty: Curl physical meaning?
cards.back: Local circulation density with orientation.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Classical Mechanics and Oscillations: What is work?
cards.back: Line integral ∫F·dr in a chosen frame.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Electromagnetic Theory: Why is field inside electrostatic conductor zero?
cards.back: Mobile charges redistribute until no field drives steady interior current in equilibrium.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Quantum Mechanics: What is an operator?
cards.back: Linear map on state space representing transformations; observables require self-adjointness/domain conditions.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Statistical Mechanics: Microcanonical constraints?
cards.back: Fixed E,V,N for isolated equilibrium system within energy shell.

cards.front: Answer in one sentence — Nuclear Physics and Radiation Protection: Main SEMF terms?
cards.back: Volume, surface, Coulomb, asymmetry and pairing.
